title: Senior Product Designer, Learner App (m/f/d)
description:
We're building a new global Berlitz, and this is your opportunity to help shape it. Nearly 150 years of expertise, meeting the ambition and technology to power a new era of learning. 

If you are the kind of person who thrives in a fast-paced environment, isn’t afraid of a blank page, and is excited to help shape the future of a global company undergoing a significant transformation, you might belong at Berlitz! 

Berlitz has taught languages for almost 150 years, mostly in classrooms and with live teachers. Now we're putting that method in people's pockets. The Berlitz app connects structured lessons, AI speaking and writing practice, 1:1 sessions with human tutors, and visible progress into one learning loop on iOS and Android. We're launching it market by market, and growing it fast.

Our learners are professionals who need a language for their career. Some pay for themselves. Others get Berlitz through their employer, who wants proof the investment is working. Both need an app they open every day because it helps them, and keep paying for because they can see themselves getting better.

As Senior Product Designer, you'll own major parts of the learner app, from the first minute after download to the moment someone books their tenth tutor session. You'll report to the Staff Product Designer for this area of the business, and partner as an equal with Product Management, Engineering, and our AI and learning experience teams.

What you'll be doing

- Design core learner journeys end to end across iOS and Android: onboarding and placement, daily learning, AI practice, tutor booking, progress, and the path from free to paid.

- Design for habit and momentum. Find out why learners come back, why they drop off, and what makes them feel progress, then build that into the product.

- Shape how learners speak and write with AI: conversational interfaces, real-time feedback on pronunciation and writing, and the moments where an AI tutor should hand over to a human one.

- Work AI-native every day. Use AI design tools and agentic workflows to explore, prototype, and produce at speed, while staying the human in the loop who decides what's good enough to ship.

- Pressure-test every PRD before it becomes a design. Question the assumptions, find the missing edge cases, and sharpen the problem with your PM, instead of passing a brief straight to a tool and accepting what comes back.

- Hold AI output to a high bar. Run rigorous evals on what AI produces for craft, accessibility, localisation, and brand fit. When you see the same problem twice, fix it at the source by updating the design system.

- Run research yourself. Talk to learners often, run usability tests, read the analytics, and set up experiments that tell us whether a change worked.

- Own the conversion and retention moments (trials, paywalls, upgrade prompts, reminders) so they earn revenue without costing the learner's trust.

- Design for corporate learners too: employer-paid access, entitlements, and the progress their company expects to see, without making the app feel corporate.

- Build with Berlitz's shared design system and help it evolve, especially the mobile patterns, motion, and micro-interactions a daily-use app needs. Keep it structured so that both people and AI tools use it correctly.

- Design for many markets and languages from the start, including text expansion, right-to-left scripts, and accessibility.

- Work closely with engineers to ship fast, then sweat the details once it's live.

What we're looking for

- Several years designing and shipping consumer mobile apps that people use every day, with a portfolio that shows native iOS and Android craft.

- Evidence that your design work moved retention, engagement, or conversion, and a clear view of how you measured it.

- Strong interaction and visual design. You care how a screen feels in the hand: motion, feedback, and pacing, as well as how it looks.

- Hands-on research and experimentation. You've run your own interviews and usability tests, and used A/B tests and analytics to make calls.

- An understanding of B2B: how a product changes when the person paying isn't the person using it, and how to serve both.

- Real experience with AI design tools (currently we mostly use Claude Design) and agentic workflows. You use tools like Claude Design, Figma Make, or Paper, and AI coding tools like Claude Code daily, and you can show examples where you rejected or reworked an AI output and explain why.

- Experience working within a design system and extending it.

- Clear communication, and the confidence to push back on PMs, engineers, and senior stakeholders with reasoning they can act on.

- Fluent English. Another language is a plus. We are a language company, after all.

- Based in Germany, Switzerland, or Hungary.

Nice to have 

- A background in a learning, language, or content app, or another product built on a daily habit (reading, audio, fitness).

- Experience with freemium and subscription models, including app store payment flows.

- Experience designing for markets in Latin America or South Asia.

- Experience taking work from AI design tools to code to the repo. That means pushing front-end changes yourself through pull requests and checking your work in iOS and Android simulators.

What we offer

- A combination few learning apps have. A recognized learning method, a global network of human teachers, and an AI team building practice and tutoring on top.

- One global Berlitz. Join a company actively rebuilding itself, with new products, new systems, and new ways of working across every team.

description:
The Firm 

XTX Markets is a leading algorithmic trading firm which uses state-of-the-art machine learning technology to produce price forecasts for over 50,000 financial instruments across equities, fixed income, currencies, commodities and crypto. It uses those forecasts to trade on exchanges and alternative trading venues, and to offer differentiated liquidity directly to clients worldwide. The firm trades over $250bn a day across 35 countries and has over 250 employees based in London, Singapore, New York, Paris, Bristol, Mumbai, Yerevan and Kajaani.

We leverage the talent of the people who work here, modern computational techniques and state-of-the-art research infrastructure to analyse large data sets across markets quickly and efficiently, to maximize the effectiveness of our proprietary trading algorithms. We are actively seeking new methods and ideas. The models that drive our trading strategies have evolved considerably over the last 10 years, from econometric methods that gave our company its name, to trees, to neural networks, to modern deep learning architectures.

XTX Markets has an unrivalled level of computational resources in the trading industry, with a growing research cluster currently containing over 25,000 GPUs with 650 petabytes of usable storage. Teams across the firm include world-class researchers, developers and technologists with backgrounds in pure math, programming, physics, computer science and machine learning. The firm is also constructing a large-scale data centre in Finland to future-proof its significant computational capabilities.

At XTX Markets technology is our business and we are a diverse organization which attracts outstanding talent from across all industry backgrounds. We are focused on teamwork, and our people collaborate on all aspects of the business, working openly and with respect for each other, our clients and the market. Our culture is non-hierarchical and one where everyone is valued. We strive for excellence in everything we do.

The Role 

As a Realtime Analytics and Controls Developer, you will be responsible for the mission control panel for one of the largest trading systems in the world ($250bn-300bn/day). Your work will have a company-wide impact, with users including Trading Desk, Trading Developers, Quants, CEO, Distribution and Risk.

The goal is to provide clarity about what our trading system (hundreds of thousands of strategies) is doing at any given moment and how it is performing. We supply both high-level and incredibly detailed views, as both are crucial for efficient decision making and spotting issues. In addition to visibility, we are also responsible for trading control mechanisms – e.g., tweaking limits, starting trading strategies or emergency stopping. These actions are necessary for continued trading, and sometimes need to be taken within minutes, with millions of pounds at stake.

Realtime Analytics and Controls is a small specialist tam which works directly with multiple front office groups. You will be expected to also contribute to the shared software platform that supports this group.

This is one of our most people-oriented engineering roles. You should expect to collaborate regularly with your colleagues who are the primary customers of your software, to understand how your design decisions affect their day-to-day work.

Responsibilities

- Understand workflows of all teams involved in trading.

- Design, implement and maintain software, including:

- An Ingestion mechanism for large volumes of data from trading systems.

- Internal frameworks for data processing and presentation.

- In-memory query engines.

- Present the data in a clear, useful, and accurate way, in collaboration with frontend developers.

- Maintain calculation of trading metrics.

- Build software that can reliably run 24/7.

- Participating in the on-call rota.

Essential Attributes 

- Pragmatic with strong ability to communicate with technical stakeholders: understanding users’ needs, soliciting features / requirements from them and prioritising effectively according to business needs.

- Algorithmically literate and able to write efficient code.

- Familiar with distributed systems – able to reason about consistency, delays etc.

- Willing to learn Kotlin.

- Skilled in writing automated tests.

- Passionate about reducing complexity.

- Deeply caring about correctness and reliability.

title: Salesforce Solution Architect
description:
Since 2004, we’ve been bringing investment ideas to life and connecting capital with the right people and opportunities. Today, we manage more than £2.5 billion for a broad range of investors across five key investment strategies: Private Credit, Social Housing, Clean Heat, Energy and Venture. These strategies underpin the innovative range of investments we offer to both private (retail) and institutional clients. 

There are 230+ employees at Triple Point, all committed to leaving the world demonstrably better than we found it. That’s why we’re a certified B Corp, signed up to the Principles for Responsible Investment, and were named a Sunday Times 'Best Place to Work 2025 & 2026' . 

I f this sounds like an environment where you would flourish, then read on… 

The Function & Team 

The Digital and Technology team's purpose is to provide cutting-edge digital solutions that are safe and reliable whilst improving efficiency and reducing potential risks for everyone at Triple Point.

The Digital Transformation team looks after our core systems, the integration between them, and all aspects of data, from the data warehouse to reporting that provides clear insight into trends. It automates manual business processes, adopts emerging technology such as Gen/Adaptive AI, and uses Microsoft 365 tooling to make TP and our TP'ers more efficient. It also manages our outsourced Salesforce developers and quality assurance specialists to ensure delivery quality and pace.

The Role 

As our Salesforce Solution Architect you are a senior member of the in-house Business Systems team and own our customer portals and the end to end journeys that run through them. Your primary remit is to design solutions that let us keep providing outstanding service to investors and IFAs through our digital channels, with streamlined and intuitive UI/UX that meets industry standards. You have ownership of what gets built and how it is delivered, and you set the governance and principles that keep our systems safe and compliant.

You own the target architecture and standards, and you make sure development across our internal team and partners follows our best practices, supported by robust DevOps and QA frameworks. The role blends requirements gathering and refinement, solution design, prototyping, and oversight of build, release and quality.

The Role’s Key Responsibilities 

Portal strategy and competitive advantage 

- Research what investors and IFAs value and how competitors serve them, review the feedback we receive, and recommend ways Triple Point can differentiate its digital services.

- Translate findings into a portal roadmap with clear priorities and measurable outcomes, and own that roadmap.

Solution design & governance 

- Provide solution design and decisioning across our suite of products - shaping and reviewing capabilities and making pragmatic day-to-day design decisions that align with our target architecture.

- Uphold data protection, security and regulatory requirements in what is designed and released - the Salesforce data model, security and sharing, data quality, and GDPR / UK GDPR and FCA obligations.

- Set and uphold development and delivery standards, champion best practices, and mentor and upskill the in-house team.

- Provide technical assurance over the delivery partner's build - review deployability, standards adherence, test coverage and quality, and hold delivery to account operationally.

End-to-end customer and colleague journeys 

- Lead the design and continuous improvement of complete journeys across our products, from initial engagement and onboarding, including KYC, through to ongoing servicing.

- Design the colleague side of every journey too, including the hand-offs between the portals, Client Operations, Client Services, Distribution and other systems, so customers never have to repeat information.

- Own UI/UX decisions for the portals, and involve investors and IFAs in pilots and feedback.

- Design self-service capabilities such as product and investment information, documents and progress updates that improve service quality while reducing effort for customers and colleagues.

Release and quality assurance 

- Set the release and quality standards the team is held to, and sign off key journeys before they ship.

- Assure test coverage and release quality across in-house and partner delivery, working with the Tech Lead who owns the release process day to day.

Testing, reliability and performance 

- Own the end-to-end test strategy for key customer journeys across products, devices, screen sizes and browsers.

- Monitor availability, response times, accessibility and journey failures, with clear ownership for resolving issues.

Security, privacy and compliance 

- Build security, privacy, GDPR / UK GDPR and FCA requirements into portal design and delivery, including the data model and sharing model, working with Cyber, the DPO and Risk.

- Lead technical investigations where required.

Prototyping and delivery support 

- Build proofs of concept and prototypes that bring new journeys to life, so investors, IFAs and colleagues can see and react to features before they are built.

- Support the development team where it counts by guiding approach, challenging design and implementation choices, resolving escalations, and stepping in with hands-on support when delivery needs it.

- Use AI tooling in day-to-day work and show how it accelerates design and delivery.

Experience 

- Significant experience designing and delivering Salesforce Experience Cloud portals for external users, including authentication, sharing, branding and responsive UI/UX.

- 8+ years in the Salesforce ecosystem, including at least 3 years in a solution architect role with demonstrable architecture and delivery ownership.

- A consulting background, or experience within a financial services or wealth management business, is preferred.

- Solution design across Sales, Service and Experience Cloud with the judgement to make and hold design decisions, out of the box first, within a target architecture.

- Financial services or regulated-industry experience, ideally with Financial Services Cloud, and a working understanding of investment and lending products such as assets under management, VCTs and ISAs, and of KYC and onboarding journeys.

- Designing end-to-end customer journeys with business stakeholders, including discovery, journey mapping, pilots and feedback loops with end customers or intermediaries.

- Translating complex Salesforce concepts into clear, actionable designs for non-technical stakeholders and developers.

- Strong Salesforce data modelling and security and sharing design, with GDPR / UK GDPR and FCA obligations built into what is designed.

- Integration design across REST, platform events and middleware, and data flow ownership between Salesforce and other systems.

- Defining test strategy for customer-facing journeys, including cross-device and cross-browser coverage, accessibility and performance monitoring.

- Setting design and development standards, leading design and code reviews, and holding a delivery partner to quality outcomes.

- Hands-on fluency in flows, Experience Cloud builder, and custom development to prototype journeys, review others' work credibly and challenge an approach.

- Practical use of AI tooling in design and delivery work.

- Experience assuring or governing third-party or partner delivery.

- Representing the Salesforce platform confidently in leadership and governance forums.

Essential Qualifications & Desirable Experience 

Essential qualifications 

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related technical discipline.

- Salesforce Certified Administrator, Platform Developer I and Platform App Builder.

- Salesforce Experience Cloud Consultant.

- Application Architect and/or System Architect (preferably both).

Desirable experience 

- Experience rolling out Financial Services Cloud and/or Financial Services Cloud Accredited Professional certification.

- Salesforce OmniStudio experience.

- Salesforce Certified Sales Cloud Consultant.

- Salesforce Certified Service Cloud Consultant.

- A DevOps tooling accreditation (e.g. Gearset or Copado).

- Integration experience with a middleware (e.g. MuleSoft).

- Data warehouse experience (e.g. Snowflake).

- A recognised data-protection / privacy qualification (e.g. BCS Foundation Certificate in Data Protection, or IAPP CIPP/E).

- Salesforce experience across Sales, Service and Experience Cloud in a regulated financial-services setting.

What Success Looks Like 

Within the first year the focus is on delivering significant improvements to our existing portals and on designing and supporting the journeys for our new products. Alongside that, you will have helped untangle data challenges across the platform, with a clearer data model and better data quality, and supported the wider business initiatives delivered by our partners so they land within our architecture and standards. The portal roadmap will have been researched and prioritised and will be in delivery against measurable outcomes, and design, development and quality standards will be applied consistently by the in-house team and our delivery partner.

In this role you will be responsible for one of THG Fulfil's largest and most complex accounts, spanning B2B/channel and B2C/D2C fulfilment, inbound and new product introduction (NPI), value-added services, systems integration, and commercial administration, with direct exposure to both client leadership and THG group executives.

The Role 

This is one of the most strategic, highest-visibility accounts in the Fulfil portfolio, and a newly created, dedicated role to match. It carries real intensity: a daily governance and reporting obligation, and a breadth of scope across B2B, B2C/D2C, inbound, NPI, VAS, integrations and commercial that effectively spans several workstreams under one relationship.

With that comes genuine ownership. The successful candidate will be THG's primary point of contact for the client's operational, logistics and programme teams, translating their requirements into internal action across warehouse operations, transport, IT/integrations, ISC and commercial — and holding those teams to delivery. They will own the account's governance calendar and daily reporting, resolve escalations end-to-end, and hold credible technical conversations on integrations without needing to do that work personally. This is a role for someone who wants to run something significant, not administer it.

Why This Role 

- Real seniority from day one: of one of Fulfil's largest and most complex accounts — you're the person in the room with senior leadership on both sides, not a supporting player.

- A genuine growth track: this account and role are being created because the business is investing in getting its biggest relationships right; strong performance here is a natural springboard toward Account Director.

- Influence, not just delivery: you'll shape governance, commercial terms and how internal teams organise around the account, rather than just following a playbook.

- Depth over breadth: rather than spread thin across a portfolio, this is a rare chance to build deep, specialist expertise across the commercial, operational and technical sides of one major account.

Key Responsibilities 

Client Relationship & Day-to-Day Ownership 

- Act as the primary THG point of contact for the client's operational, logistics and programme teams, including their EMEA fulfilment, transportation, global service & logistics and extended workforce (xWF) partners.

- Run a weekly 1:1 with the client account lead, plus regular ad hoc syncs with programme and technical contacts, translating requirements into internal actions across warehouse operations, transport, IT/integrations, ISC and commercial — and holding those teams to delivery.

Governance & Reporting 

- Own the account's governance calendar, including MBRs, QBRs, daily hypercare calls, and weekly ops, VAS, D2C & Inbound and PM check-in calls — a minimum of two hours of scheduled client contact every working day before reporting, escalation handling or project work.

- Produce supporting evidence packs for dispute resolution, and supply data extracts on request.

Escalation & Incident Management 

- Own live, cross-functional escalations end-to-end, keeping internal teams coordinated and the client informed throughout.

- Provide same-day resolution and communication to the client and THG executives, including outside standard hours when escalations land on weekends.

Systems & Integration Oversight 

- Maintain working fluency in EDI and integration concepts sufficient to triage issues and hold credible technical conversations with the client's technical teams, without doing the integration work personally.

- Support ongoing platform and project work including THG portal development, Fulfil UI change requests, and client-specific ISC process fixes, demos and training.

Project & Change Delivery 

- Lead delivery of account-specific projects and programmes (e.g. VAS/device rework programmes, NPI set-up, dangerous-goods order flow, EMEA programme initiatives) working across warehouse, transport, IT and ISC.

Commercial Support 

- Lead commercial alignment sessions on activity outside the standard rate card (e.g. non-SSCC handling, decant, space over-allocation, DG printing), providing the operational evidence base for commercial and compliance discussions.

Requirements 

- Client-facing account management experience in third-party logistics or supply chain, ideally with enterprise technology or consumer electronics clients.

- Strong data and reporting capability — able to build compliance and performance reporting from raw operational data without analyst support.

- Working understanding of EDI and integration concepts (945s, SSCC, IMEI and serialised stock, ASN flows) sufficient to triage issues and hold a credible technical conversation.

- Confident operating at executive level on both sides of the relationship, including under escalation.

- Able to influence internal operational teams without direct line authority across warehouse, transport, IT, ISC and commercial teams.

- Build and screen plasmid libraries, and develop the cloning workflows that let us do it at scale;

- Contribute to an open and high-integrity scientific culture at Basecamp Research;

- Establish strong documentation practices and lab SOPs as a founding member of the lab team.

Required Skills and Experience

- A PhD in molecular biology, biochemistry, genetics, bioengineering, or a life-sciences related field, or an MSc with equivalent hands-on laboratory experience.

- Experience with gene editing, NGS assay development, protein engineering and cell therapy;

- Experience with high-throughput methods of cloning and producing DNA constructs for cellular screening;

- Experience with mammalian cell culture, transfection, and cell-line generation;

- Knowledge of emerging technologies in gene editing and on/off-target analytics that enable regulatory approval;

- Expertise with DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, ddPCR, NGS library preparation and QC

- Excellent communication skills to both internal and external stakeholders

Advantageous Skills and Experience

- Experience contributing to a preclinical cell therapy program (in vivo or ex vivo);

- Expertise in flow cytometry using both antibody panels and fluorescent reporters;

- Experience developing novel methods for gene editing off-target analytics using both long and short-read sequencing;

- Mechanistic understanding of gene editing tools, including nucleases, base editors, transposons, retrotransposons, and recombinases; Ability to reason about proteins as molecular machines;

- Experience integrating AI protein design tools with high-throughput wet lab screening methodologies;

- Fluency in NGS instrumentation, basic bioinformatics tools, and traceable data pipelines.

- Proactive Problem-Solving: A proactive, resourceful, and independent mindset. You take initiative to identify problems or inefficiencies and act on them. You’re the kind of person who spots an issue and rallies the right people to fix it before it escalates.

- Adaptability: Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid change. Our environment evolves quickly – you should thrive in a dynamic setting and be flexible in adjusting plans, while maintaining a positive, can-do attitude.

- Ownership & Drive: High degree of ownership over your work. You care about outcomes and reliably follow through on tasks and take pride in delivering quality results.

title: Controller
description:
About Notabene

Notabene is building infrastructure that's transforming how money moves in the digital economy. We're evolving beyond our compliance foundations to enable the next generation of digital financial services between regulated institutions with unprecedented efficiency. With nearly 50 employees across 14 countries and having recently closed our Series B round last November with support from leading investors including Y Combinator, DRW, F-Prime, Jump Capital, Castle Island, and Green Visor Capital, we're looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry.

Location: 

US-based, Remote East Coast

The impact you will have

Notabene is planning on going through its first external financial statement audit, covering the fiscal years ending January 2026 and January 2027. You will own that process. You will also own the close, the books, and the accounting policy for a two-entity, multi-currency business whose revenue includes subscription fees, usage-based transaction billing, and a payments network take rate that has no clean accounting precedent anywhere.

The accounting function is already substantially built. Close runs, the books are in order, and readiness work for the audit is well underway. What we need is someone to own it, finish it, and take it through the audit, while raising the standard on policy and documentation as the business gets more complex. You will be the most senior accounting voice in the company, reporting to the VP of Finance, with one direct report and a set of external providers. You will not have a large team before late 2027, and that is deliberate. Capacity here comes from better systems and better automation, and you will be the one deciding what those look like.

Within a year you are successful if

- Notabene has a clean audit opinion on both fiscal years, with no material weaknesses and no second cycle on auditor requests

- The close hits its calendar consistently, starting with the revenue close landing on time

- Revenue recognition is documented in a written memo that stands up in fieldwork, rather than living only in the billing system configuration

- Multi-entity consolidation and FX translation run cleanly enough to survive audit scrutiny, with intercompany and CTA tied and supported

- Payroll allocation across departments and software development capitalization are written policy applied consistently, not judgment applied after the fact

- Key accounting controls are documented, operating, and evidenced

- At least two accounting processes that are manual today run without a person in the loop, and still hold up under audit

What you will be doing

Audit. Run the readiness assessment, build the remediation plan, contribute the technical view on which firm we engage, and then own the auditor relationship day to day.

Close and reporting. Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close across Notabene Inc. and Notabene GmbH. Produce GAAP financial statements, consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and FX translation under ASC 830.

Technical accounting. Write the positions and the memos. ASC 606 across three revenue models, ASC 350-40 for internal-use software capitalization, ASC 718 for stock compensation expense, and whatever emerges as stablecoin payment revenue matures.

Revenue and billing systems. Own Tabs as the billing and revenue system of record, including contract configuration, usage data integrity, and the bridge from Tabs to the general ledger.

Cost accounting. Build the payroll allocation method for people whose work splits across functions, and the capitalization policy for development work, so departmental margin reflects where effort actually goes.

Controls. Design and implement controls over revenue, cash, procure to pay, and payroll. Not SOX. Controls that operate, are evidenced, and can be walked by an auditor.

Automation. Evaluate the accounting stack and the processes running on it with a bias toward automation, including agentic tooling where work is rule-bound and high volume. Categorization, reconciliation matching, usage validation, and collections follow-up are the obvious places to start.

Accounting operations. Own AR and collections with your direct report, plus AP and payroll accounting. Employee onboarding and HRIS administration sit with People, not with you.

Tax. Own US tax compliance in coordination with our external advisers, including the income tax provision and sales tax. Coordinate Swiss compliance with our local accountants.

External providers. We produce revenue in-house, our Swiss accountants produce their piece, and our outsourced firm assembles the close. You will own the checklist, the policies, and the reconciliations, so providers execute against a Notabene-owned close rather than holding it themselves.

description:
CreatorIQ is the operating system for creator-led growth trusted by more than 1,300 global brands and agencies.

We’re on a mission to make businesses more human, and humans more impactful. We operate by our values — be intentional, pursue excellence every day, embrace the journey together, and be a good human — every day. CreatorIQ has earned the title of best companies to work for in multiple programs, including BuiltIn LA and NY. It’s been named a Fastest-Growing Company in North America on the Deloitte Technology Fast 500™ for four years, was named a leader in IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Influencer Marketing Platforms for Large Enterprises in 2025, was named a Leader by The Forrester New Wave™: Influencer Marketing Solutions, and has been consistently recognized by G2 as a Leader, and is rated 5 stars on Influencer MarketingHub. We operate in a flexible work model that combines both in-person and remote work to boost collaboration, enhance innovation, and adapt to individual work styles.

We're seeking passionate, innovative minds to join our journey. Be a part of our dynamic team and let's transform the industry together!

Product Manager, Safety & Compliance 

CreatorIQ is the software enterprise brands and agencies use to run their creator marketing programs. Customers include Burson, Delta Air Lines, Google, LVMH, Nestlé and Sephora. Those programs only hold up if the content is brand safe, sponsorships are disclosed, the music is cleared, and every campaign follows the rules in the markets it runs in. You'll own the product that makes that happen.

The core is SafeIQ, our always-on brand safety system. It runs multimodal AI classification on audio, video, images and text across millions of creator posts, and flags risk before it becomes a headline.

If you like turning messy classification and regulatory problems into workflows that risk, legal and compliance teams trust, you'll fit in. We're growing fast, and we work with teams around the world who care about doing great work.

In this role, you’ll get to: 

- Own the in-app brand safety review and workflow experience end to end, with one goal: shorten the path from "AI flagged something" to "a human made a confident decision." Ship, measure, learn, repeat.

- Decide how AI classification reaches people: severity, categories, thresholds, review states and false-positive handling. Work with data science on what the models look for across audio, video, images and text, how confident they need to be before surfacing something, and where a human stays in the loop. Make every flag explainable and auditable.

- Own compliance beyond content risk: sponsorship and ad disclosure under FTC guidelines and their equivalents, music licensing and rights clearance, legal drinking age (LDA) rules for alcohol promotion, and GDPR and regional privacy requirements. Work with Legal, Trust & Safety and regional compliance stakeholders to stay ahead of regulatory change without making every workflow wait on a legal review.

- Understand the business nuance for API contracts, webhook payloads and data models with engineering so customers can pull safety and compliance signals into their own systems.

- Work with GTM on positioning, packaging and enablement so what we sell matches what the product does and what regulators require.

Who you are and what you’ll need for this position: 

- You've spent 4+ years in product management or equivalent technical product ownership in B2B SaaS. Titles matter less than the work.

If you’re looking for a place where you can do more, be more, come grow with us.

As a Machine Learning Engineer, you'll join our Personalize team, helping shape and build the products that let our customers personalise messages across every digital touchpoint. You'll work with text data and with cutting-edge technologies including Large Language Models (LLMs), bringing Accessible Intelligence to our customers across both Personalize and Optimove's overall platforms.

This is a role for an engineer who's ready to own meaningful, medium-sized pieces of our personalisation roadmap end-to-end - from problem framing through to deployment and monitoring - and trusted to do so with minimal oversight. It's not solo delivery: you'll be working closely with a dynamic team spanning ML, MLOps and software engineering, and should be happy to contribute at every level, from early-stage research through to production support.

Role & Core Responsibilities 

- Own the delivery of medium-sized ML features end-to-end within Personalize - problem framing, data preparation, model build/train, evaluation, deployment and monitoring - to predictable timelines.

- Develop predictive ML models for classification, ranking and personalisation, working with our text data.

- Leverage LLMs and other state-of-the-art techniques to enhance product capabilities.

- Operationalise models as APIs across real-time and batch environments.

- Monitor production models in your own scope, treating data quality issues and model degradation as a priority.

- Research new ML applications and improve pre-existing models, sharing findings with the wider ML, MLOps and engineering team.

- Collaborate closely with product, MLOps and engineering teams to define and prepare new ML applications, contributing meaningfully to planning and grooming.

- Proactively surface and resolve technical and data challenges before they affect delivery, model quality or customers.

Best Bits of the Job 

- Exposure to a wide range of ML domains, including large-scale search, ranking, Natural Language Processing, hybridisation, classification and text data processing.

- Working with modern ML technologies, including LLMs, to enhance our products.

- Fully real-time architecture for data processing, model development and deployment.

- Deploying and enhancing ML frameworks, optimising for inference and training/retraining cycles.

- Online testing of models with live data, using our proprietary A/B/N testing technology to see quickly what performs well.

- A supportive, collaborative team spanning ML, MLOps and software engineering, where rapid experimentation is the norm.

- Dedicated time to research new methods, build proofs-of-concept, and ship to production quickly when they work.

- Everyday use of modern AI coding assistants (e.g. Claude) to speed up experimentation and review.

Essential Requirements 

- Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics or a related field, OR 1–4 years' professional experience building and deploying ML models.

- Strong understanding of core ML concepts - supervised/unsupervised learning, model evaluation, feature engineering - and broad familiarity with common algorithms and architectures.

- Strong Python (pandas, NumPy, etc.) and SQL skills

- Comfortable with the standard ML toolkit: Git, Docker, scikit-learn, PyTorch or TensorFlow, and ML pipelines.

- Hands-on experience with text data and relevant Natural Language Processing techniques.

- Solid experience with cloud technologies and data storage solutions, including Snowflake.

- Everyday use of AI coding assistants (e.g. Claude), and a basic understanding of responsible AI practices - data privacy, bias/fairness and explainability.

- Must be eligible to work in the UK – we are unable to provide sponsorship at this time

- This is a Hybrid role, and you will be required in our Dundee office two days per week. 

Desirable Requirements 

- Understanding of personalisation across domains such as sports betting and gaming, and what best practice looks like there.

- Full understanding of recommendation algorithms and their applications.

- Professional experience in personalisation and/or predictive CRM, and micro-segmentation.

- Experience with CI/CD pipelines and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools (Terraform, Bicep, etc.).

This role sits on the in-role path towards Senior Machine Learning Engineer. As you grow, you'll deepen your expertise in our core ML stack, take on end-to-end ownership of larger features, represent the team in cross-functional planning with MLOps and software engineering.

description:

At Nscale, you’ll help shape how customers adopt next-generation AI infrastructure. You’ll work with fast-growing AI companies and enterprise organisations, support strategic customer engagements, and play a visible role in translating Nscale’s technical capabilities into commercial success.

You’ll be joining a company at the forefront of GPU cloud infrastructure, with the opportunity to influence customer outcomes, product feedback loops, and go-to-market execution. This role offers the chance to combine technical depth with real commercial impact.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
Senior Product Manager

Location: UK (remote)

Job Description 

About Us 

Reachdesk is the first truly end-to-end global SaaS gifting and swag platform, helping B2B companies create meaningful connections with prospects, customers, and employees, while driving measurable ROI.

We believe gifting is more than just a transaction: it’s about building genuine human connections that fuel business growth. Whether it’s engaging prospects, celebrating customers, or recognizing employees, our platform makes it easy to deliver personalized gifts, branded swag, and unforgettable event & brand experiences at scale through automated sourcing, storage, and global delivery.

Trusted by many of the most recognized names in technology and SaaS, Reachdesk integrates effortlessly with marketing, sales, and HRIS tech stacks and is powered by our world-class team across New York, London, and Lisbon.

We’re growing, and we’re currently looking for a Senior Product Manager to join us.

About the Role 

As a Senior Product Manager at Reachdesk, you’ll play a pivotal role in shaping the Reachdesk Platform. You will be accountable for turning complex customer and business problems into software products that deliver measurable impact.

Reporting to the Chief Product Officer, you’ll lead product initiatives end-to-end, from identifying and deeply understanding the right problems to solve, through discovery and delivery, to launch, adoption, and continuous improvement.

You’ll operate with a high degree of autonomy, proactively building context across customers, the market, internal stakeholders, data, and technology to understand what Reachdesk needs to achieve its goals. You’ll also make sound decisions when the path forward isn’t obvious.

You’ll partner closely with Engineering and Design and work across the wider business to create alignment, communicate decisions clearly, and ensure what we build is successfully launched, adopted, and delivers the outcomes we set out to achieve.

If you enjoy solving difficult problems, taking ownership, and moving comfortably between customer, technical, and business conversations, you’ll thrive in this role.

Responsibilities 

- Set product direction and priorities , bringing together company goals, internal stakeholder needs, customer insight, market context, data, and technical considerations to focus on the highest-impact opportunities.

- Define problems and experiences before solutions , creating clear stories, journeys, and shared context so the Design and Engineering teams understand the problem and intended outcomes before determining the solution.

- Lead product initiatives end-to-end , from discovery and solution definition through delivery, rollout, and iteration, partnering with Engineering to manage scope, make pragmatic trade-offs, and deliver valuable solutions at pace.

- Make sound product decisions and trade-offs , balancing customer and business needs, commercial impact, user experience, and technical considerations while aligning the wider business on compromises, priorities, and expectations.

- Develop product opportunities with external partners , building relationships with technology partners to uncover mutual opportunities, shape integrations, align roadmaps, and navigate the product and commercial considerations required to bring them to market.

- Orchestrate successful launches and adoption , working across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Services, Logistics, Finance, Legal, and other teams to ensure the business is ready and customers realise value from what we build.

- Communicate with clarity throughout , ensuring leadership and teams across Reachdesk understand product decisions, progress, risks, changes, and results.

About you 

- You have a strong track record of owning B2B SaaS products end-to-end , from identifying the right problems through delivery, adoption, and measurable customer and business outcomes.

- You’re a strong problem solver who gets to the root of complex problems, brings structure to ambiguity, and uses evidence and judgement to determine the right path forward.

- You operate with independence and initiative : you seek out the customers, stakeholders, data, and context you need rather than waiting for direction, while staying anchored to Reachdesk’s goals and priorities.

- You have strong business and commercial awareness and are curious about how the wider company operates, allowing you to understand competing needs and make pragmatic decisions beyond the boundaries of Product.

- You’re technically fluent enough to work effectively with Engineering , understand systems, integrations, and constraints, ask the right questions, and contribute meaningfully to solution and scope decisions.

- You’re an exceptional communicator , able to create clarity, influence decisions, surface difficult trade-offs, and adapt how you communicate across customers, engineers, leadership, and teams throughout the business.

- You’re comfortable operating externally as well as internally , building productive relationships with technology partners, uncovering shared opportunities, influencing without authority, and navigating product, technical, and commercial conversations.

- You have a strong sense of product and user experience , caring about the coherence and quality of the complete experience rather than whether individual requirements or features have simply been delivered.

The benefits 

- Competitive salary with generous stock options

- Pension with employer contributions (NEST)

- Affordable Private Medical Insurance, including mental health support and fast access to care

- Flexible PTO that increases the longer you’re with us, plus extra flexibility for life’s unexpected moments

- A genuinely collaborative culture with innovative, fun, and ambitious people

Reachdesk believes that a diverse team helps us achieve our mission faster, and so we welcome applicants from all backgrounds. 

Privacy Policy: We process personal information submitted as part of your application in accordance with the Reachdesk Candidate Privacy Notice. Please review Reachdesk’s Privacy Policy here: www.reachdesk.com/candidate-privacy-policy

The Data Science team at CoMind develops the algorithms and machine learning systems that transform raw optical interference signals from CoMind One into continuous, clinically meaningful measurements of cerebral blood flow, intracranial pressure, and autoregulation. Working at the frontier of photonics, physiology, and applied ML, the team's work directly determines what CoMind One can measure, how accurately, and under what clinical conditions.

As Principal Data Scientist, you will be a technical authority for CoMind's data science function, setting methodological direction for signal condition and extraction, personally driving the most complex and highest-impact problems, and providing expert guidance on data science best practice across the team. This is a senior individual contributor role: you will not manage people directly, but your technical leadership will shape how the entire team approaches its most challenging problems. - Act as the technical authority for the end-to-end signal processing and inference chain for CoMind’s technologies: from raw optical data through to clinical measurements

- Set the methodological direction for estimation, signal extraction and ML modelling across the team: which approaches suit which problems, how they are evaluated, and what evidence is required before a method is trusted.

- Own signal processing and analysis programmes from research through to validated, production-quality implementations with Software Engineering.

- Derive achievable performance bounds from instrument and noise models, and use them to drive algorithm selection, requirement setting and design trade-offs

- Own how the team handles uncertainty and calibration — inference methods appropriate to small clinical cohorts, per-patient estimation with quantified uncertainty, and calibration strategies that make measurements comparable across devices, sessions and patients.

- Set the standard for how the data science function works: reproducibility, analysis and code review, experiment design, dataset governance and ground-truth definitions

- Act as the primary technical reviewer and expert resource across the research organisation, reviewing technical reports, analysis plans and evaluation methodology, and holding the bar for methodological rigour and scientific integrity.

- Identify and introduce new, best-practice methods from estimation, inference and measurement science in adjacent fields.

- Act as a mentor to members of the Data Science teams and across the wider business

- Contribute to CoMind's IP and publication strategy, authoring and reviewing technical papers, patent applications and regulatory documents.

AI is fundamental to our culture. It's not just a tool, but a core part of how we work, collaborate, and innovate. We expect all team members to embrace AI in their daily work and continuously find new ways to use it effectively.

Skills & Experience: 

- 15+ years of experience in data science, ML, or applied research, with a strong track record of independent technical leadership on complex, ambiguous problems

- A career working to extract small signals from noisy, complex physiological systems, and developing and deploying physical models of those systems to support those efforts.

- Deep expertise in physiological time-series signal processing methodologies.

- A demonstrated ability to take algorithmic work from research concept through to production-quality, validated implementations in shipped product.

- Designing device performance evaluation methods where no prior gold-standard exists: simulating physical systems, running sensitivity analysis, identifying failure modes, and developing signal processing solutions to address those challenges.

- Extensive experience owning calibration and cross-instrument comparability work that involved noise models, error budgets, and evaluation of experimental data

title: Chief Business Officer (gn) @ Clean Data Centres Venture, France (hybrid)
description:
This is an Atlantic portfolio company. 

Why we exist 

Every frontier model is now gated by two things: megawatts and cooling . Grid queues stretch for years, land is contested, freshwater is political.

Far offshore, the wind blows stronger and steadier than anywhere on Earth, a vast resource the grid can, by definition, never reach.

So we flipped the problem. Instead of bringing power to the load, we bring the load to the power. Our autonomous wind-turbine energy ships chase the wind across the open ocean and convert it on board into what the world needs most: compute first, then e-fuels to decarbonise aviation.

- 70%+ capacity factor — offshore wind that behaves like baseload

- ~€50/MWh target cost for firm, low-carbon power

- Zero grid queue. Zero freshwater. Zero land. And the ocean as the heat sink under every rack.

Founded in 2025 by repeat entrepreneurs (with successful exits) and industrial operators. Backed by major international investors. First demonstrator vessel at sea in late 2027.

The role 

This is not a sales job. It's a late co-founder seat. You will own Offshore Compute , our first and main commercial engine: strategy, product, pricing, customers and the multi-million-dollar off-take deals that put our first fleet to work.

You already know that power and thermal limits are what will stall AI scaling. You're bold enough to believe infrastructure at sea can get around both, and rigorous enough to prove it to a sceptical buyer.

What you'll do 

- Write the go-to-market from a blank page. Build the global commercial roadmap, from first demonstrator workloads to full fleet monetisation.

- Land the anchor deals. Negotiate and close off-take agreements, capacity reservations and JVs with neoclouds, AI labs, CSPs and Tier-1 HPC operators.

- Turn variable power into a feature. Design offers built for wind-backed power profiles: fault-tolerant batch training, asynchronous inference, dynamic pricing, zero-carbon AI clouds.

- Connect the C-suite to the hull. Translate client requirements (SLA, latency, direct-to-chip liquid cooling) into onboard architecture specs together with our marine engineers.

- Create a category. Use our advantages — no grid wait, no freshwater, a direct ocean cooling sink, very low carbon intensity — to win premium pricing and long-term commitments, and establish floating compute as a new asset class.

- Be the face of it. Represent us at the top AI, cloud and infrastructure summits worldwide and make us the reference for next-generation AI energy infrastructure.

You might be the one if 

- You've been in the room where AI capacity gets bought. You've sold, built or run serious infrastructure in the neocloud, AI infra, CSP or hyperscale data center world, and you've closed the kind of deals that move megawatts. We care about what you've shipped, not what your business card said.

- You know GPU economics inside out. H100 / B200 / GB200 cluster economics, orchestration, workload constraints. And you know the people across the neocloud and AI ecosystem who sign capacity deals.

- You speak the physics. MW-scale power delivery, PUE, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, thermal budgets. You can explain in one slide why land-based data centers are hitting the grid wall.

- You've built something from zero. You've scaled a business line, closed complex multi-million infrastructure contracts and thrived with high autonomy and high ambiguity.

- The ocean pulls at you. You care about climate, and standing on the deck of a floating compute lab during sea trials sounds like the best day of your year.

- You work in English. Fluent English is required. French is a bonus.

How you operate 

- Owner, not operator. You don't wait for a playbook. You write it.

- Maths over rhetoric. When a buyer is sceptical about offshore compute, you open the energy and thermal maths.

- Realistic madness. You have the conviction to break paradigms and the engineering and commercial discipline to deliver.

- Humble and brave. You stay intellectually humble and still take bold positions, especially where conventional playbooks fail.

- AI-native. You use modern AI tools for maximum leverage while keeping the domain authority to negotiate directly with C-level executives.

What's in it for you 

- A founding-team seat with executive terms, shaping the company and not just a function

- A real shot at creating a new asset class at the intersection of AI, energy and the ocean

- A small, uncompromising team of entrepreneurs and industrial leaders, backed by top-tier capital

- Flexible hours, a base in Nantes and a mandate that spans the globe

title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Search (remote, Europe)
description:
Hey, I'm Adrian . I’m hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join the Data Search team at Modash.

Modash helps brands find, understand, and work with creators across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. More than 2,700 companies—including Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN—use us to manage and scale their creator partnerships.

Behind that product is a fascinating search problem: helping customers find the right people across 400M+ creator profiles and billions of media files. We’re combining large-scale data processing, traditional retrieval, vector search, multimodal embeddings, and LLMs to make that possible.

That’s where you come in.

Why we're hiring

Search at Modash isn't an internal platform or a support function. It is one of the core products customers use to discover creators.

The scale is large, the data is messy, and the search intent is often complex. A customer might be looking for creators in a specific niche, people whose content conveys a certain visual style, or accounts that resemble a group they already know. Solving that well requires more than adding another filter or calling an LLM API.

We need a senior engineer who can work across the full retrieval system—from data and indexing pipelines to embeddings, ranking, relevance, and low-latency serving—and take ambiguous product problems all the way to production.

You’ll join the specialised Data Search team and work closely with Data Core, Data Insights, product teams, customers, and company leadership. You’ll have real autonomy, but you won’t work in isolation.

If you want a feel for how we think about building software, check our Engineering Blog .

What you'll actually own

1. Make creator search meaningfully better. 

You’ll improve how customers discover creators across 400M+ profiles and billions of media files. That includes retrieval, filtering, ranking, relevance, speed, and the product decisions that connect them.

2. Turn multimodal data into searchable intelligence. 

You’ll build systems that generate and use embeddings from images, video, text, and audio at massive scale—then make those signals useful in a real customer-facing search experience.

3. Ship new search capabilities into production. 

You’ll evaluate models and technologies pragmatically, understand tradeoffs around cost, latency, and quality, and move promising approaches from experiment to a reliable production system within weeks rather than quarters.

4. Own the system end to end. 

You’ll help shape the problem, gather requirements, design the architecture, write the code, release it, measure the outcome, and improve it. Senior engineers here own results, not just implementation tasks.

What the day-to-day looks like

Here’s what a typical week might include:

- Monday. A customer search is returning technically relevant but unhelpful results. You inspect the retrieval and ranking stages, identify where intent is being lost, and propose a measurable improvement.
- Tuesday. Deep-focus time. You build a pipeline to generate multimodal embeddings across a large batch of creator content and test how the new representation affects retrieval quality and cost.
- Wednesday. You work with Data Insights on a new in-house datapoint. Together, you agree on its definition, coverage, and data-quality requirements, then expose it in Search to give customers more ways to discover creators.
- Thursday. You test a reranking model on a fixed set of real customer queries. You measure how much it improves relevance against the latency and inference cost it adds, then decide what's ready for production.
- Friday. You review production metrics, investigate a relevance regression, and share what you learned with the team. The fix may be in the model, the data, the query logic, or the product itself—you follow the evidence.
We keep meetings purposeful and protect time for deep work. You’ll have a short standup, close collaboration when it helps, and plenty of space to design, build, optimise, and launch.

Requirements 

What you've done before

- Built large-scale data or backend products. You have solid experience working with systems where volume, latency, reliability, and cost all matter.
- Shipped products from concept to production. You’ve owned scoping, architecture, implementation, release, measurement, and iteration—not just one layer of the solution.
- Designed distributed systems. You can reason clearly about throughput, failure modes, data flow, scalability, and operational tradeoffs.
- Built LLM-powered or agentic features in production. You understand the practical differences between models and can balance capability against latency and cost.
- Worked autonomously on ambiguous problems. You know how to gather requirements, ask useful questions, and turn incomplete context into forward motion.
- Communicated clearly across teams. You can explain technical tradeoffs to engineers and non-engineers, give direct feedback, and collaborate without creating unnecessary process.
- Worked in a fast-moving product environment. You’re comfortable learning quickly, shipping incrementally, and changing direction when the evidence does.
Bonus points if you’ve worked with multimodal embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, ranking algorithms, model deployment, self-hosted models, or GPU infrastructure. Curiosity about the creator economy helps too, but we’ll get you up to speed.

Our stack

- AWS and GCP, with Pulumi for infrastructure as code
- Python, TypeScript, and Node.js
- PySpark on AWS EMR
- Airflow
- Milvus Vector DB through Zilliz
- Elasticsearch
- LLM batch APIs
- Apache Iceberg
- SageMaker, DynamoDB, S3, Glue, Kinesis, Lambda, ECS, and Aurora
- Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Cursor
The interview process

We move quickly and can complete the process in under a week:

- Intro chat
- Coding interview
- System design interview
- Team interview
- Culture and alignment conversation with our CEO, Avery Schrader
Benefits 

What we offer

- Fully remote in Europe 🏠 Work from wherever you do your best work, with some overlap with GMT+3.
- Compensation. Your compensation is made up of salary and stock options. As we're growing fast, the stock option package is especially significant. Annual salary range is 100,000€ - 130,000€ for this role. We hire across Europe, so the exact number depends on your location, employment type, skills, and experience.
- Flexible hours ⏱ We care about outcomes, not when you log on.
- Unlimited paid vacation 🌴 If you’re rested and happy, you do better work. Take what you need.
- Personal development support 🧠 Courses, books, and conferences are on us when they help you grow.
- Real ownership 💡 Take difficult search problems from idea to production without layers of unnecessary process.
- Regular offsites ✈️ We’re remote-first, but we make time to connect, collaborate, and have fun together in person.

And a little more about us...

Founded in 2018 by a high-school dropout and a Canadian (yes, we’re also shocked it’s going so well), Modash is building a suite of tools that help brands scale partnerships with online content creators.

2,700+ companies like Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN already use Modash to manage and scale their influencer marketing work. And we're just getting started. Over the coming decade, brand investment in creators will continue to boom, and Modash will be at the centre of it all.

Modash is here to stay. We have 8-figures in ARR across two products, a $12M series A investment , and we are default alive. We are building a company that will still be here in 20 years; not rushing towards an exit.

We’re almost 100 people distributed across 20+ countries, operating with a fast, async-first culture. If you join Modash, you’ll be surrounded by people who truly want to be the greatest at their craft. People who make you better. Interesting people too, who have done everything from building solar cars, to hanging out with Metallica and Bon Jovi.

Come join us. Be great, do great things, create great memories, all while making a great impact. Do it.

title: Move to New Zealand - Technical Strategist (Solution Architect)
description:
Work alongside our innovative team based in Auckland, New Zealand! We are seeking talented individuals excited about the opportunity to learn, expand their skillset and support our company. 

We welcome applications from individuals located internationally looking to relocate to Auckland, New Zealand. This role is based in Auckland and requires in-office attendance (hybrid). 

Propellerhead hires exceptional talent from all around the globe and many of our people have relocated to New Zealand to join our team. We've created this website packed full of information about moving to New Zealand to work for Propellerhead, if you're interested in making the move to our wonderful country. 

Prior to applying, please be aware that the final stage of our recruitment process is an in-person interview in New Zealand (click apply and see our application questions for more details). 

The Role: 

At Propellerhead, the Technical Strategist role focuses on the delivery of resilient software systems that power everything from complex infrastructure to innovative new platforms. This role works alongside our Product Strategists to shape the technical specification and platform direction for a portfolio of client products.

We’re looking for someone who combines architectural insight with a strong hands-on engineering background and a genuinely AI-native way of working. You will have spent the formative part of your career as a software developer and still be confident with understanding the structure of software solutions. You'll have knowledge of emerging trends and you are agentic-first where you reach for AI to rapidly prototype new ideas and judge their value in hours, not weeks, and you are at home with directing an AI-assisted delivery pipeline.

You will lead and guide the design of complex systems, and we'll depend on your extensive experience, judgement and insights to ensure that early delivery and continuous improvement is possible. You’ll be applying and reinforcing Engineering standards for programming, and shape the technical solutions our AI-assisted pipeline builds, in a lean and evolutionary manner. Importantly, you will be responsible for ensuring that client platforms align with our technical strategy. You will work closely with the Chief Technologist and Engineering Principal to apply standards, patterns, and tooling in client contexts, and provide informed input into technical strategy through client platform insights and delivery experience.

Propellerhead operates a hybrid working model (work from our office and from your own home). While you must be based in Auckland for this role, we warmly welcome applications from across New Zealand and internationally who are planning to relocate to Auckland. This particular role requires regular in-person office attendance.

We offer a culture built on trust, continuous learning, and meaningful impact. You'll join a team that values integrity over ego, and clarity over complexity.

If you're looking to contribute your insight and engineering experience to projects that matter - we would like to hear from you.

Skills & Experience Required: 

- 8+ years of experience with the development of multi-tier and distributed applications. 

- Agentic-first: very comfortable using AI to rapidly prototype, shape solutions, and direct an AI-assisted delivery pipeline across requirements, testing and code generation. This is central to the role.

- A confident, credible communicator and presenter in front of senior client stakeholders.

- Our current technologies include React user interfaces, with services written in C#, so previous experience with both is essential. However we also have Typescript, Java, Go and Rust services, so you will need to show confidence in working with a variety of programming languages.

- Strong communication skills must be demonstrable, with tangible examples of your skills to bridge technical solutions with business needs and present these concepts to a variety of internal and customer stakeholders. 

- Hands-on experience with designing solutions on Azure is essential, including active participation in building CI/CD pipelines and instrumenting for operations, is required.

- Experience with streaming and messaging platforms, such as Kafka or NATS, is highly desirable.

- Proven experience in leading the design of complex software applications, preferably for corporate enterprise, where solutions comprise existing services alongside custom development.

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. You will represent Propellerhead in front of stakeholders, so a professional, confident presence and the ability to communicate and influence with clarity are essential.

- We are particularly looking for technical leaders with experience or demonstrable interest in any of the following: digital identity, verifiable credentials, open banking, AI agent authorization, edge or device-based software deployment.

Responsibilities: 

- Authoring, reviewing and communicating solution architecture and specifications in collaboration with the Development teams and our core Engineering team.

- Championing the technical strategy of Propellerhead as our key business differentiator, and aligning design and implementation of the solutions in your portfolio in line with that technical vision.

- Building trusted relationships with key client decision-makers. You will be responsible for ensuring our teams understand technical requirements and for clearly explaining our solution design to client technologists.

- You will be the go-to technical person for our client’s solutions, including facilitating any technical pre-requisites for delivery or addressing improvements from operational feedback.

- Developing strategies to ensure quality measures such as speed-to-value, security, reliability, maintainability, performance and functional fit for purpose.

- Specifically, you will be facilitating the evolution of our code base from C# to Rust and the ecosystem of tools, practices and services that implies, with AI central to how we handle requirements, testing and code generation.

About Propellerhead: 

Propellerhead is a leading software services company that designs, delivers, and maintains large-scale, custom-built digital platforms across a range of technologies. We place emphasis on producing technology which is meaningful, has value, and can make a difference in the world. We foster long lasting and trusting relationships with all our clients. Over our 20+ years in the market we have worked with a diverse range of commercial, non-profit, and government organisations.

How We Build Software: 

We build software by structuring solutions in a product-centric manner and focusing on continuously delivering measurable outcomes into production. Our work starts from real stakeholder needs and the value they unlock, with an AI-assisted pipeline now generating much of the code.As a result, our digital platforms are a mixture of custom components and external services which produce a powerful and engaging experience when combined.

Benefits: 

- 
Be part of an innovative team, with a culture of learning and collaboration.

- 
Contribute to interesting, diverse, and commercially minded work for well-respected clients.

- 
Opportunity for professional growth and development.

- 
Fortnightly knowledge sharing sessions, with lunch.

- 
Competitive salary. Employee Share Purchase Scheme offering.

- 
This role is Auckland based, regular in-office attendance is required. Work within our beautifully designed office and from home (hybrid working model).

- 
Propellerhead is an equal opportunity workplace which is free from discrimination.

Cover Letter: 

*Please note - only applications with a cover letter will be reviewed. 

It's very important to us that you include a cover letter with your application - it's your chance to tell us more about who you are and what you value.

At Propellerhead, we use AI thoughtfully as part of our delivery practices - considered integration helps us stay at the forefront of technology and create innovative, valuable solutions for our clients. 

In recruitment, however, AI isn’t used to assess skills, experience or suitability for a role. Every application is reviewed by a real person to ensure a fair, engaged and thoughtfully human process.

Cash flow is the fuel behind every hire we make and every GPU we spin up — and right now, that process runs on scrappy startup instincts more than scalable systems. We're hiring an AR Specialist to change that: someone who can take full ownership of collections, chase down what's owed without losing the relationship, and build the reporting and processes that let Finance actually see around corners. You'll sit at the intersection of Finance, Sales, Operations, and Customer Success, which means your work is never just about invoices — it's about making sure the whole revenue engine runs cleanly as we scale. If you get real satisfaction from replacing chaos with a system that just works, this role was built for you.

- Run the full Account Receivable lifecycle — invoicing, payment tracking, account reconciliation

- Watch aging reports like a hawk and chase down outstanding invoices before they become a problem

- Keep customer account records clean and resolve billing discrepancies fast

- Support month-end close for everything AR and cash application related

Drive collections and cash flow 

- Design and execute collection strategies that shrink DSO and speed up cash collections

- Build real relationships with customer AP teams — the kind that get payment delays resolved with a phone call, not an escalation

Build the systems, not just run them 

- Use collections tools to automate outreach and track performance — this isn't a spreadsheets-forever role

- Partner with Finance leadership to level up AR processes, reporting, and controls

- Work with Sales to make sure billing is accurate from the first invoice

- Help build the scalable AR playbook a high-growth startup actually needs

Report on what matters 

- Put together weekly AR aging and collections reports for leadership

- Track DSO, collection effectiveness, and overdue balances like they're your own scorecard

- Support audits and keep documentation clean for compliance

Qualifications/Nice to haves:

- 3+ years in Accounts Receivable, Billing, or Collections

- Comfortable in a SaaS, tech, or startup environment

- Solid grasp of AR processes, collections strategy, and cash application

- Experience with an ERP/accounting system

- Strong communicator and negotiator — genuinely fine picking up the phone and calling a customer

- Organized, detail-obsessed, and good at juggling deadlines when things move fast

- Hands-on experience with Tesorio or similar AR automation/collections platforms

- Experience supporting enterprise or B2B customers

- Familiarity with SaaS billing models, contracts, and revenue operations

- Comfortable using AI tools to speed up analysis and reporting

title: Product Manager Intern - Connect
