Founded in 2012, Mirakl has been at the forefront of marketplace innovation, empowering every business to compete in the platform economy.

Today, Mirakl's operating system combines an enterprise marketplace solution (Mirakl Platform) that enables retailers and B2B organizations to launch, scale, and operate marketplaces and dropship, AI-powered multichannel selling (Mirakl Connect), retail media (Mirakl Ads) and an agentic commerce infrastructure (Mirakl Nexus).

With dual headquarters in Boston and Paris, Mirakl helps a global ecosystem of 450+ marketplaces (B2C and B2B) and a network of over 100k third-party marketplace sellers. Brands like Macy's, Decathlon, Carrefour, Asos, and Airbus Helicopters use Mirakl to grow their businesses in new and remarkable ways.

For more information: www.mirakl.com .

Mirakl in Numbers: 

- 🗓️ Founded in 2012 | Member of French Tech Next40

- 👥 750+ employees in 9 offices worldwide: Paris, Barcelona, Bordeaux, Boston, London, Munich, New York, Sydney, Tokyo

- 🇫🇷 350+ Mirakl Tech teams members mainly based in France

- ⚙️ 5 Saas Solutions

Our Values: 

Working at Mirakl means accelerating your career alongside ambitious, passionate, and supportive colleagues. We're proud of the diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences that make our teams unique.

Our 5 values guide how we collaborate:

- 💡 Work Hard Together: Teamwork and collaboration are the foundation of our success

- 🏆 Get Things Done: We prioritize action and efficiency for impactful results

- 🚀 Go Above & Beyond: We tackle challenges proactively and always aim for excellence

- 🎓 Succeed Through Expertise: Knowledge sharing and continuous learning are core to our culture

- 🤝 Satisfy & Empower Clients: We're committed to our clients' success

The Team You'll Join 

You'll join the Product team of Mirakl Connect, the platform that helps brands and sellers grow their sales across marketplaces and other sales channels. You'll work closely with the VP Product Connect, the Channel Integration PM and the whole Channel Integration squad.

This is a 6-month internship starting in January 2027. You'll participate in team rituals, gain autonomy progressively, and have the opportunity to present your work regularly to management, offering strong visibility within the organization.

Your Impact 

Choosing and building the right channels is one of our biggest growth levers. As a Product Manager Intern, your mission will be to help the team prepare and assess new channel opportunities, reduce uncertainty before development starts and contribute to successful integrations.

Your work will help the squad bring together the key information, questions, risks and opportunities before development begins.

Concretely, you will:

- Help pre-qualify channels: Map the marketplace landscape by country and vertical, and contribute to a first-level assessment of each channel: technical integration effort, functional coverage with Mirakl Connect, and business potential (seller demand).

- Explore channel requirements: Review channel API specifications and requirements across catalog, offers, orders and logistics, and test them hands-on (e.g. with Postman). With support from the team, identify key questions, dependencies, risks and areas that require further investigation.

- Prepare build-ready inputs: Turn your analyses into useful inputs for the squad, such as data mappings, process diagrams, edge cases, open questions for channel partners and first drafts of user stories."

- Talk to the field: Interview sellers, Sales and Customer Success teams, and channel partner teams to turn scattered feedback into clear insights and product recommendations.

- Contribute to channel builds: Alongside the Channel Integration PM and the squad, help refine specifications and user stories, contribute to backlog discussions, answer functional questions and participate in QA and go-live preparation.

- Build AI-powered tools to scale channel work: Use AI tools to accelerate research, analysis and prototyping. For example, you may help create an agent that analyzes channel documentation, a Q&A assistant for Sales and Customer Success or AI-assisted prototypes to explore mappings and integration flows.

What Success Looks Like 

- After 3 months: A broad set of channels pre-analyzed at a high level, with a first assessment of technical integration effort and functional coverage, contributing to channel pre-qualification

- After 6 months: Several channels analyzed in depth and handed over to the squad as build-ready, an active contribution to channel builds, and at least one AI tool in daily use by the team

What You'll Bring to the Role 

Profile & Experience 

- Currently pursuing a gap year internship or end-of-studies internship (engineering school, business school or university)

- Strong interest in e-commerce, marketplaces and retail

- A structured mindset, with the ability to turn a broad or ambiguous question into a clear and actionable analysis

- A genuine curiosity for understanding how products, processes and systems work

- Previous experience in a start-up or scale up, in e-commerce, consulting, business analysis or project work is a plus, but not required

Technical Skills 

- Hands-on with APIs: You understand what an API is and how systems exchange data, and you can read API documentation and make simple API calls (e.g. with Postman). Familiarity with data formats (JSON, XML) or integration concepts is a plus.

- Data and spreadsheet skills: You are comfortable using spreadsheets to analyze, compare and synthesize information. Experience with dashboards or SQL would be a plus.

- Hands-on with AI tools: You use AI tools daily and critically to improve research, analysis and product work. Experience creating prompts, automations or agents is a plus. 

Soft Skills 

- Curious, proactive and rigorous: You take initiative, ask thoughtful questions and dig until the key unknowns are clarified.

- Strong communication and collaboration skills: You communicate clearly with different stakeholders, collaborate effectively in cross-functional environments and can summarize complex information into clear, actionable conclusions for different audiences.

- Fast learner with adaptability: You pick up new domains quickly and are comfortable learning unfamiliar concepts.

- Critical thinker: You can challenge assumptions, assess the quality of information and distinguish facts from hypotheses.

Languages 

- Fluent English is mandatory, both written and spoken, as it is our working language with the team and channel partners.

- Another European language is a plus.

Compensation 

Monthly stipend range: €1,200 - €1,400

Our Hiring Process 

We warmly encourage you to apply to this role, even if you think you're not an exact match.

Please click the "Apply" button to submit your application. This helps us make the best possible assessment and get back to you as quickly as possible.

- Manual screening of your CV by a recruiter and then an AI-powered screening conversation (10 min) with Emma, Mirakl's AI Talent Ambassador to explore your background and motivation for the role. You will need to complete this step within 3 days, otherwise we won't be able to move forward with your application

- TA interview (30-45 minutes) to discuss your experience and answer your questions about Mirakl

- Hiring Manager interview (45 minutes) with one of the Product Managers to dive deeper into the role and assess technical fit

- STAR interview (45 minutes) to evaluate alignment with our values and team culture

- Offer

We welcome collaborators with their diverse perspectives and experiences to power us forward. These often far exceed conventional job requirements and help us create a culture of continuous learning. If you're ready to join a global leader powering digital transformation for 450+ of the world's most innovative retailers and B2B organizations.

You can exercise your data protection rights at any time, and as further detailed in our policies. title: Sales Development Representative (SDR) - Scale up Healthtech
description:
Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales ont le potentiel de transformer le système de santé. Mais seulement si elles sont accessibles. Plus de données accessibles → moins de charge administrative, une meilleure coordination des soins et des découvertes scientifiques plus rapides.

Depuis 2015, notre mission est de libérer ce potentiel. Nos solutions basées sur l'IA permettent aux professionnels de santé de partager les informations médicales sans effort et aux chercheurs d'accélérer les découvertes cliniques : avec un impact sur des millions de patients en France chaque jour. Alors que nous nous préparons à nous développer en Europe, 2 choses déterminent notre succès : nos équipes et notre mission.

Aujourd'hui, plus de 150 personnes travaillent depuis nos bureaux et à distance pour libérer le potentiel des données de santé. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé, et nous ne faisons que commencer. Nous recherchons des personnes qui embrassent la complexité, veulent résoudre des problèmes difficiles et sont prêtes à construire le futur de la collaboration en santé.

⚡ Notre équipe Sales Public 

L’équipe Sales Public accompagne les établissements de santé dans l’adoption des solutions Lifen, principalement autour de la gestion des documents de santé. Elle compte aujourd’hui 8 Sales Account Executives qui travaillent sur l’ensemble du territoire.

Les Sales concentrent aujourd’hui leur temps sur les plus grands établissements et groupements hospitaliers. À côté, il existe un vivier d’environ 800 structures de santé de plus petite taille. Leur potentiel est réel, mais le CRM est encore peu qualifié et les bons interlocuteurs restent souvent à identifier.

Nous créons donc notre premier poste de SDR Public. Ton rôle sera de construire ce périmètre : mieux connaître ces structures, trouver les personnes à contacter, qualifier les opportunités et transmettre aux Sales des rendez-vous réellement exploitables. Tu travailleras principalement sur nos offres Lifen Documents et Curecall by Lifen.

🎯 Ce que tu feras chez nous 

- Cartographier et prioriser un portefeuille d’environ 800 petites structures de santé, en partant d’une base CRM encore largement à enrichir.

- Identifier les bons interlocuteurs au sein de ces établissements, en mobilisant les informations disponibles sur Internet, LinkedIn, le téléphone et les autres canaux de prospection.

- Entrer en contact avec les prospects, comprendre leur contexte et qualifier les opportunités avant de proposer un échange avec un ou une Sales Account Executive.

- Générer des rendez-vous qualifiés pour l’équipe Sales, en transmettant les informations utiles pour permettre une prise de relais efficace.

- Mettre à jour le CRM avec rigueur : contacts, informations sur les structures, niveau de maturité des opportunités et prochaines étapes.

- Faire progresser les méthodes de prospection sur ce nouveau périmètre : messages, séquences, critères de qualification et priorisation des comptes.

- 

⭐️ Ce que nous recherchons 

Must-have

- Une première expérience commerciale (Stage, Alternance ou CDI), idéalement d’un à deux ans en startup, en SDR, Inside Sales, prospection B2B ou relation client.

- Une vraie appétence pour la prospection : prendre contact, obtenir les bonnes informations, relancer et transformer une approche en rendez-vous qualifié.

- La capacité à organiser un volume important de comptes, à prioriser et à tenir un suivi précis dans un CRM.

- Une communication orale et écrite claire, adaptée à des interlocuteurs de direction de structures de santé.

Nice-to-have

- Une expérience dans la santé ou auprès de professionnels et d’établissements de santé.

- Une première expérience dans un environnement startup ou scale-up.

- La pratique d’outils de CRM et de prospection.

Soft skills

Tu es énergique et tu aimes avancer sur un périmètre à construire. Face à une base peu qualifiée, tu sais chercher, trier l’information et décider par où commencer, sans te disperser. Tu communiques simplement, tu écoutes avant de proposer un rendez-vous et tu acceptes les retours pour ajuster ta manière de faire. L’humilité compte : tu travailleras avec une équipe Sales expérimentée et tu sauras apprendre à ses côtés tout en apportant tes propres observations du terrain.

Nos valeurs

Embrace Complexity . Tu avances dans un secteur de santé complexe et sur un portefeuille encore peu structuré, en transformant progressivement des informations éparses en opportunités qualifiées.

Bienveillance . Tu collabores étroitement avec les Sales, dans une équipe où l’entraide et le partage d’informations font partie du quotidien.

Real Impact. Chaque rendez-vous qualifié peut contribuer à équiper davantage de structures de santé avec des outils qui simplifient la circulation des documents.

👥 Process de recrutement 

Le process est volontairement court et se déroulera principalement en visio.

- TAM Screening avec l’équipe recrutement - Environ 30 minutes. L’objectif est de comprendre ton parcours, ta motivation pour le poste et d’évaluer les fondamentaux attendus : communication, énergie, organisation et posture commerciale.

- Case study avec l’équipe Sales - Un entretien en visio d’1h comprenant la restitution de trois exercices : deux préparés à l’avance et un exercice réalisé en direct. Le cas sera envoyé environ deux jours avant l’échange et demandera environ 1h30 à 2h de préparation. Il permettra d’évaluer ta capacité à qualifier un compte, à prioriser, à structurer une approche de prospection et à communiquer avec clarté.

- Final Interview - Un entretien avec un Manager de l’équipe Sales pour valider l’alignement culturel.

Nous nous engageons à te donner de la visibilité tout au long du process et à revenir vers toi sous 72h après chaque étape. Des prises de références pourront être demandées en fin de process, avec ton accord.

Soigner mieux en soignant ensemble, c'est aussi agir avec bienveillance. À l'image du secteur dans lequel nous évoluons, nous favorisons la diversité, l'inclusion et l'équité. Nous mettons en valeur vos compétences et votre savoir-faire, et bannissons toute forme de discrimination, qu'elle soit sexuelle, religieuse ou politique.

You own the code that runs in the factory.

What We're Looking For - 5+ years building geometry-heavy software in production - CAD/CAM, geometry kernels, feature recognition, CAE/simulation preparation, metrology, or comparable.
- B-rep and Mesh Depth . You think natively in topology and NURBS. Feature recognition, defeaturing, robust booleans, offsetting, surface/surface intersection, healing and repair. You know exactly why floating-point robustness destroys naive implementations - and what to do about it. You have had the opportunity to delve into complex CAD models and are able to assess their quality in both quantitative and qualitative terms (gaps in edge, spikes in loops, tiny elements, twisted surfaces...) and ultimately predict which types of processing might be challenged.
- Kernel Fluency . Hands-on with a geometry kernel - Parasolid, OpenCASCADE, ACIS, or equivalent - and the judgment to know which parts can be developed in-house in order to retain full control and IP rights, and which parts too complex (e.g. advanced solvers) should be integrated as 3rd parties. Comfortable with mesh and point-cloud processing (libigl, Open3D, CGAL, PCL) alongside solid modelling.You know well STEP file format and about integration into collaboration & interoperability processes.

- End-to-End Ownership . Algorithm design through to a shipped, tested, maintained service.
- First Principles Thinker. You reason by physics and mathematics, not analogy. When an algorithm fails on a real part, you know whether the bug is in the code, the model, or the assumption.
- Industrial Grit . You want to stand next to the machine in Germany and watch your output run. The feedback loop between your code and cutting metal is the point.
- Maniacal Urgency . Speed is our only edge. You thrive in the "chaos-to-order" phase of a startup.

- Engineers who are uncomfortable with ambiguity or rapidly changing priorities.

- The Environ ment : Access to a 8,000 m² state-of-the-art facility featuring 5-axis CNCs, industrial robots, and industrial 3D printers. Your algorithms run on real hardware from day one.

- Location : Zurich HQ, with occasional time at Factory ONE in Munich.

Apply Resume : Focus on geometry systems you've built and owned.
GitHub/Portfolio : Show us the hard problem you solved - code, papers, or parts that came off a machine because of you.

title: Senior Robotics Software Engineer - Autonomy Architecture
description:
Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots. 

Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment. 

Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. 

The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously. Increasingly, we also build custom hardware to adapt our machines for highly specialized, robust applications beyond traditional excavation. 

About the Job 

The autonomy team at Gravis architects autonomous behaviors for different tasks, e.g. different types of excavation or truck loading. This role owns the architecture that lets those behaviors live in the same software stack as opposed to creating one SW stack per behavior. You'll be responsible for how tasks are decomposed and orchestrated, for the interfaces between, and for the software quality. We are looking for a senior roboticist with C++ and Python expertise and high standards for software quality, who can make clear, pragmatic architectural calls that let the system grow without losing stability.

What you'll do 

Architecture 

- 
Own the task-level architecture shared across our autonomous behaviors

- 
Define clear module boundaries and responsibilities between behavior orchestration, factor out common logic across different tasks

- 
Implement component tests and telemetry/metrics collection pipelines

- 
Identify technical debt early enough to guide the team toward sustainable solutions

- 
Act as the go-to person for software quality: modern C++ practices, code structure, error handling, robustness. Likewise for Python.

Configuration & tooling 

- 
Design an easily extensible and testable module for deploying policies that can be reused across tasks and supports schema versioning for observations, so a deployed policy pins the exact version of the computations it was trained against

- 
Provide technical leadership on C++ and Python tooling (clang-tidy, sanitizers, static analysis, linting, typing, test setup)

- 
Work with our incoming simulation team to unify training, benchmarking and evaluation tooling across tasks, so adding a task doesn't mean forking tooling and infrastructure

What we're looking for 

Required 

- 
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

- 
5+ years developing complex C++ systems, with deep knowledge of modern C++ (17 and onwards)

- 
Strong Python for tooling, configuration and simulation-side scripting

- 
Strong experience designing large, modular software systems that outlived their first use case

- 
High standards for software quality and long-term maintainability

Nice to have 

- 
Experience with behavior trees, state machines, or other task orchestration frameworks in production

- 
Experience working alongside learned controllers in a production stack - deployment, versioning, observation pipelines. No need to train them.

- 
Motion planning, geometric algorithms, or spatial data structures

- 
Feature-flagged deployments, staged rollouts, or long-lived platforms

This role is a great fit if… 

- 
You want to make systems work reliably in the real world, and enjoy thinking through the edge cases

- 
You'd rather our next behavior be a configuration than a dedicated piece of software

- 
You want the best idea to win regardless of who had it, and you'd rather be corrected by the numbers than agreed with

- 
You take a result end-to-end: when something needs to happen, you use or ask for whatever it takes, even outside your scope

- 
You're a software purist, but pragmatic — first make it work, then make it right, and cut corners consciously when it's the right call

title: Technical Marketing Engineer
description:
The role 

Neural Concept is looking for a Technical Marketing Engineer to turn emerging engineering technologies into compelling demonstrations, technical content and joint partner stories.

You will explore how Neural Concept can work with technologies from partners, primarily NVIDIA, and prototype new engineering workflows. You will then translate that work into strong demos, videos and articles that make our technical depth tangible to the market.

You will turn the work into a technically credible article explaining the method, findings and implications.

This role sits within Marketing and works closely with Product Marketing, Partner Marketing, Research, Product, Engineering and our Vertical Solutions teams.

Your mission 

Make Neural Concept’s technical capabilities visible and understandable.

You will combine hands-on engineering work with strong market judgement. You will start with the audience and the story we want to tell, then build the right prototype or content to prove it.

The goal is to create credible and visually strong demonstrations of what becomes possible when Neural Concept connects with emerging AI and engineering technologies. These are marketing prototypes, not production-ready integrations. They must communicate the concept clearly and remain technically accurate.

What you will do 

Drive technical co-builds with partners 

- Explore partner technologies and identify where they can create new engineering workflows with Neural Concept.

- Lead technical co-build initiatives, with an initial focus on the NVIDIA ecosystem, including technologies such as PhysicsNeMo, Warp, Omniverse and agentic frameworks.

- Build prototypes that combine Neural Concept capabilities with partner products and infrastructure.

- Work directly with partner technical and marketing teams to shape joint stories.

- Turn technical exploration into demos, videos, event content and other co-marketing assets.

- Identify new opportunities for joint content, launches and market visibility.

Produce technical marketing content 

- Write technically grounded articles, explainers and demo narratives.

- Create and present demos for partners, events, campaigns and executive conversations.

- Develop demo scripts and work with design or video specialists to produce polished assets.

- Repackage internal prototypes and engineering work into content that external audiences can understand and remember.

- Help Product and Partner Marketing communicate technical mechanisms precisely, without unnecessary complexity.

Build for the audience 

- Define the audience, message and desired outcome before starting technical work.

- Make deliberate choices about what needs to work end to end and what can remain a prototype.

- Prioritise a clear story, strong visual execution and market relevance.

- Simplify the experience without oversimplifying the technology.

- Validate technical claims with the relevant internal experts before publication.

What we are looking for 

- A strong engineering background

- The ability to build technical prototypes independently. Experience with Python and AI or engineering software is strongly preferred.

- Knowledge of one or more relevant areas: machine learning, physics AI, simulation, CAD/CAE, geometry processing, engineering software or agentic systems.

- Evidence that you can explain technical subjects through writing, demos or video.

- A marketing-first mindset. You think about the audience and the intended reaction, not only the technical implementation.

- Strong visual and product judgement. You care about how a demo looks and how clearly it communicates value.

- Comfort working with external technology partners and coordinating across technical and marketing teams.

- The ability to move quickly through ambiguity and build enough to prove a concept.

- Excellent written and spoken English.

This role may suit you if 

- You are an engineer who has repeatedly moved towards storytelling, demos, content or developer marketing.

- You want to influence how a deep-tech company presents its capabilities to the market.

- You prefer building a convincing prototype and narrative over maintaining production systems.

- You can challenge a technically impressive idea when it does not serve the audience or the message.

- You optimise technical work without considering how an external audience will understand it.

- You see writing, storytelling and visual presentation as tasks to hand over after the engineering work is complete.

- You are uncomfortable making pragmatic trade-offs when building exploratory prototypes.

How the role complements Product Marketing 

Our Product and Technology Marketing function owns the broader product narrative, positioning and business value. The Technical Marketing Engineer brings deeper hands-on engineering capacity.

The two roles work together: Product Marketing defines the story and market context; the Technical Marketing Engineer explores the technology, builds the proof and contributes the technical content.

What success looks like 

Within the first year, you will have:

- Established a repeatable technical co-build motion with NVIDIA and other priority partners.

Power electronics are the bottleneck on every next-generation UAS airframe we build: motor controllers, gate drivers, and DC-DC stages are what define flight time, payload, thermal envelope, and field reliability. We're looking for a senior IC to own the analog power chain end-to-end across our UXV platforms: from MOSFET commutation simulation through PCB layout to lab validation. You will be the technical reference on power electronics inside our Lausanne engineering hub, unblocking propulsion, airframe, and embedded teams in parallel as we scale from prototype cadence to multi-platform deployment.

This is a builder role, not a research seat. You ship hardware.

Responsibilities 

- Power Stage Architecture: Lead motor-controller and DC-DC topology across fixed-wing, multicopter, and hybrid UXV platforms. Translate mission constraints into power-chain specification.

- MOSFET Commutation & Gate-Drive Design: Own the analog switching design: dead-time tuning, gate shaping, switching-loss vs EMI vs thermal trade-offs.

- Multi-fidelity Simulation: Deploy the full stack: analytical loss budgeting, transient SPICE (LTspice), system-level modelling in PLECS or Simulink.

- BLDC Drive Stages: Design three-phase inverters with integrated current sensing, protection, Trapezoidal and FOC-aware hardware interfaces.

- High-Power-Density PCBA: Lead schematic and layout in Altium or KiCad with thermal, parasitics, and EMC engineered in from the first revision.

- EMI / EMC Engineering: Drive pre-compliance, filter design, and root-cause debug under flight-representative loads.

- Prototype-to-Production: Take motor-controller PCBAs through revision discipline, DFM, and qualification - closing the loop on field returns.

- Lab Validation: Execute bench characterization (power analysers, oscilloscopes, thermal imaging, double-pulse testing) and reconcile against simulation.

- Firmware & Controls Interface: Partner with embedded and propulsion on FOC tuning, current-sense calibration, and the hardware/firmware compensation boundary.

- Design Authority & Mentorship: Set the bar via design-decision records and reference designs. Mentor 1–2 junior engineers.

Candidate Requirements 

- MSc or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or equivalent.

- 5+ years of hands-on R&D experience on motor drives, BLDC/PMSM controllers, or high-power-density power electronics.

- Deep working mastery of MOSFET commutation design : gate-driver selection, dead-time tuning, switching transitions, loss budgets.

- Proven ownership of at least one motor-controller PCBA shipped from prototype through production (or pre-production qualification) : ideally on drone, robotics, eVTOL, or automotive platforms.

- Fluency in simulation (LTspice, PLECS, or Simulink) and PCB design (Altium).

- Strong, hard-earned intuition for EMI / EMC design and debug.

- Lab-bench discipline: you've personally debugged what simulation missed.

- Comfort with scale-up iteration speed and end-to-end ownership.

- English fluent (working language); French is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.

Bonus points for: GaN / SiC experience, safety-critical design exposure , applied control theory implemented in hardware, exposure to defense, aerospace, or UAS programmes.

title: Network Developer
description:
Senior Network Developer 

About Share 

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months.

Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served.

The Role 

Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.

You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.

What you'll do 

- Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.

- Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.

- Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.

- Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.

- Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.

- Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.

- Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.

- Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.

Our Ideal Candidate 

- 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP.

- Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit.

- Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense.

- Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.

- You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe.

- You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed.

- AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't.

- You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network.

- A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders.

Nice to have 

- Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale.

- Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them.

- Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling.

- 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification.

- Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it.

- Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America.

- DDoS mitigation at the edge.

If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway.

Compensation & Benefits 

Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a venture-backed company (US-incorporated, with a Kenya operating entity)

title: Network Operation Engineer
description:
Network Operations Engineer

1. About the role

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it.

For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar.

We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling.

The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes.

You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it.

2. What you'll do

Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing.

Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with.

Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state.

Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online.

Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed.

Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift.

Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far.

3. Who we're looking for

A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for.

Must-have

- Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong.

- Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told.

- Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge.

- Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus.

- Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you.

- Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher.

- Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly.

- Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time.

- Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day.

Nice-to-have

- CCNP, or MikroTik MTCNA / MTCRE.

- Prior NOC, ISP, or carrier operations experience.

- Hands on with MPLS (L3VPN, EVPN) and the multi-tenant isolation a shared backbone needs.

- Exposure to open source and white box routing or forwarding stacks (SONiC, IP Infusion OcNOS, FRR, or similar).

- Network source of truth and automation tooling (Nautobot, NAPALM, Jinja config generation, NETCONF or gNMI).

- Familiarity with a monitoring stack such as Zabbix, Grafana, Loki, or Prometheus, and with flow telemetry.

- Working familiarity with FreeRADIUS, CoA and Disconnect flows, and how session control and accounting hook into the network.

- Exposure to applying ML or AI in network operations: anomaly detection, predictive failure analysis, automated triage or remediation.

- IPv6 and dual stack exposure, and internet exchange operations (looking glass and route server behaviour, IRR and RPKI hygiene).

4. What we offer

- A seat inside a serious, very senior network team , with people who have deep service provider backgrounds and will sharpen you fast. You will see how a real carrier network behaves under live conditions.

- A front row seat to how a network actually gets run in 2026. Open source forwarding, config as code, and an LLM layer doing real operational work. Not a slide about the future of network operations, but the environment you would work in every shift, and help build.

- Real engineering, not just monitoring. The role is built so the quiet hours go into automation, propagation and health work, and tickets off the board. The path into deeper network engineering and automation work is the plan, not a vague someday.

- Competitive salary and private health and wellness benefits , fully remote, in a mission driven, investor backed company building the backbone of Africa's next generation internet.

description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

About the role

Delta builds BLP’s core software: the technical foundation that everything else at the company runs on.

Who we're looking for

Modelling logic and correctness by construction is paramount to us. We aim to express what must be true, prevent invalid states, and keep systems pristine even as they grow.

Thus, we’re looking for highly ambitious engineers who can tackle difficult problems and think precisely. title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Planning & Navigation)
description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will make our robots navigate dependably across real customer sites. Our stack works. The gap between working and dependable is the whole job. Every new site tests how a robot understands its surroundings and chooses where to go: a ramp the planner avoids, a narrow passage that exposes a poor route, a gate that changes the map, a person who steps into the robot's path, or localization drift that builds over a long patrol. You treat those cases as the real navigation problem to solve, not as edge cases.

You'll shape the technical choices behind reliable navigation, from sensor selection, ground segmentation, and traversability estimation to predicting how people and vehicles move and planning safe, efficient routes around them. The system has to work day and night, in challenging weather, across different embodiments and changing site conditions. We measure success by whether the robot completes its patrol on a live site, not by how it performs in simulation.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

- Navigation and path-planning design: how robots represent traversable space, select routes, avoid obstacles, and reach goals across complex sites.

- Sensor integration driven by navigation requirements, including what ground segmentation and traversability estimation need in day, night, and challenging weather.

- Environment understanding: how the robot distinguishes ground from obstacles and estimates which terrain is safe and practical to traverse.

- Behavior prediction: anticipate how people, vehicles, and other dynamic obstacles will move, and plan routes that stay safe and efficient around them.

- Field reliability: reproduce failures from deployments, find the root cause, and fix it at the right layer, from sensor data and maps to costmaps, planners, and recovery behaviors.

- Planning under imperfect localization: plans that stay useful when the state estimate drifts and the robot must execute routes in tight or dynamic environments, working with the rest of Robot Autonomy on localization and control.

- Validation on real robots: logs, simulation, and repeatable field tests to verify that design choices and changes hold across routes, lighting, weather, and site layouts.

- New autonomy capabilities: work with the engineers building the operator application and backend so operator requests and new robot capabilities rest on a sound navigation design.

- The field feedback loop: work closely with forward-deployed engineers to turn site issues into bugs, design changes, and improvements to the navigation stack.

- Regular site visits to build a practical understanding of how robots and sensors behave in real operating conditions.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for an engineer who has taken a robotics system from unreliable to dependable and takes ownership beyond individual tickets. You can explain why you made a navigation design choice and what it costs. When a robot takes a bad route, you can tell whether the planner, the map, the state estimate, or the robot's behavior is at fault, and you fix the right one. You are comfortable in the field and want to understand how robots behave in real customer environments.

YOUR BACKGROUND:

- A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Proven track record building and deploying navigation on ground mobile robots in the real world (3+ years or equivalent depth).

- Hands-on experience with mobile robot navigation and path planning: route or local planning, static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, costmaps, or recovery behaviors.

- Understanding of how mapping and localization affect navigation, and the ability to diagnose when a planning issue is actually caused by the map, the state estimate, or robot behavior.

THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will build and own the state estimation that tells our robots how they are moving and where they are. You'll fuse data from IMUs, cameras, LiDAR, GNSS, and platform-specific odometry into accurate, real-time estimates that support reliable autonomy day and night, across different robot platforms.

This is a builder's role first: you'll use the estimation methods and tools best suited to the problem, then do the engineering needed to make them work on real robots. title: Sales Engineer, Banking
description:
Fireblocks is the company bringing global finance onchain. Backed by over $1 billion in capital, we are the premier digital asset infrastructure provider trusted by thousands of industry-defining financial institutions, including banks, payment providers, fintechs, and global corporates such as BNY Mellon, BNP Paribas, ANZ Bank, Western Union, Stripe, and Revolut. Built for institutional scale and security, our enterprise-grade platform and network have powered over $14 trillion in digital asset transfers worldwide.

About the Role 

The Sales Engineer, Banking is a technically credible, commercially aware member of the EMEA SE team, responsible for the full technical sales cycle across banking opportunities in Western and Central Europe.

This is not a generalist SE role. You will be expected to engage deeply with treasury operations leads, custody technologists, CISOs, and risk committees inside Tier 1 and Tier 2 banks. You will need to understand how institutional banking technology works — core banking platforms, custody and settlement infrastructure, ISO 20022 and SWIFT messaging, and post-trade workflows — and be able to position Fireblocks clearly within that context. You will work closely with Banking-aligned Sales Directors across your region, taking primary responsibility for technical qualification, PoC delivery, RFP responses, and solution design from first engagement through to onboarding handoff.

What You'll Do 

Technical Pre-Sales 

- Lead technical qualification for banking opportunities, distinguishing genuine digital asset programmes from exploratory noise

- Deliver tailored product demonstrations to technical and executive audiences across custody, settlement, treasury, and compliance use cases

- Scope, design, and deliver Proofs of Concept in bank environments — including navigating infosec review, sandbox provisioning, and API integration testing

- Produce and own RFP, RFI, and DDQ responses for banking prospects, maintaining accuracy against Fireblocks' external security and compliance attestations

- Present Fireblocks' security architecture to CISOs, CROs, risk committees, and product and business line leads with appropriate institutional credibility

Solution Design & Client Engagement 

- Translate institutional banking requirements — custody flows, settlement logic, treasury management, regulatory reporting — into Fireblocks solution architectures

- Engage directly with bank technology teams on API integration patterns, core banking middleware, and operational workflow design

- Co-develop technical account plans with Sales Directors, identifying the path from initial engagement to production deployment

- Contribute to deal strategy on competitive situations, particularly against technology-first custody competitors

Cross-Functional Contribution 

- Act as the voice of the banking client in internal product and roadmap discussions

- Contribute reusable technical content — solution briefs, reference architectures, PoC templates — that scale across the Banking vertical

- Support onboarding handoff to Professional Services, ensuring continuity from sales into delivery

- Participate in the EMEA SE enablement programme, contributing to banking-specific sessions and peer knowledge transfer

What You'll Bring 

- 3–8 years in a pre-sales, solutions engineering, or technical consulting role, selling into or supporting Tier 1 or Tier 2 banks, financial market infrastructure, or capital markets firms

- Direct experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles in regulated financial institutions

- Demonstrable track record of scoping and delivering PoCs or technical pilots in bank environments

- Experience authoring RFP/RFI responses and engaging with bank procurement, legal, and infosec processes

- Exposure to digital asset, tokenisation, or blockchain initiatives whether from a technology vendor, infrastructure provider, or within a bank's innovation function

Technical Knowledge 

- Working understanding of institutional banking architecture: core banking platforms (Temenos, Finastra, Murex, Calypso or similar), custody infrastructure, or post-trade settlement systems

- Familiarity with financial messaging standards: ISO 20022, SWIFT MT/MX, or equivalent settlement and payment protocols

- Comfort with API-led integration patterns; able to engage credibly in technical discussions with bank engineering and middleware teams

- Understanding of cryptographic key management concepts, hardware security modules, or MPC/TSS architecture (formal training provided)

- Awareness of MiCA, DORA, or equivalent EMEA regulatory requirements as they affect digital asset operations in banks

Skills & Attributes 

- Credible with senior institutional stakeholders CISO, CTO, Head of Digital Assets, treasury operations leads, and product and business line owners — not only with technical teams

- Structured, precise communicator: able to write clearly, present confidently, and adapt register for technical and non-technical audiences

- Commercially aware: understands deal economics, qualification discipline, and what constitutes productive SE engagement

- Self-directed and organised, capable of running multiple active opportunities simultaneously without close supervision

- A European language an advantage

title: Working Student Global Licensing (DACH) (all genders)
description:
Über tonies: tonies ist die weltweit führende interaktive Audio-Plattform für Kinder mit mehr als 10 Millionen verkauften Tonieboxen und 125 Millionen Tonies. Das intuitive und preisgekrönte Audiosystem hat die Art und Weise, wie kleine Kinder unabhängig spielen und lernen, durch seinen kindersicheren, kabellosen und bildschirmfreien Ansatz verändert. Tonieboxen wurden bereits in über 100 Ländern aktiviert, und das Portfolio umfasst rund 1.400 Tonies in mehreren Sprachen. Seit der Gründung hat tonies bedeutende Meilensteine erreicht, darunter die Börsennotierung an der Frankfurter Wertpapierbörse im November 2021 sowie ein global aufgestelltes Team von über 550 engagierten Experten, die aus verschiedenen Ländern agieren. 

Teil unseres tonies-Teams zu werden bedeutet, an einer inspirierenden Mission mitzuwirken: innovative und bedeutungsvolle Erlebnisse für Kinder auf der ganzen Welt zu schaffen. Gemeinsam gestalten wir die Zukunft des Spielens, Lernens und der Fantasie. 

Du als Teil von tonies: Bei Tonies Licensing haben wir es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, die Magie von Audio zu Kindern überall auf der Welt zu bringen. Wir suchen eine motivierte und begeisterte Studentische Nachwuchskraft (m/w/d), die unser Portfolio an globalen Lizenzkonten unterstützt und dabei hilft, internationale Lizenzprojekte von der ersten Idee bis zum finalen Produktlaunch voranzutreiben. Diese Rolle ist perfekt für jemanden, der wertvolle Praxiserfahrung in einem kommerziell ausgerichteten Umfeld sammeln möchte – an der Seite eines Teams, das Beziehungen zu großen internationalen Lizenzgebern der Spielzeug- und Unterhaltungsbranche in Nordamerika und der EMEA-Region betreut. 

Deine Aufgaben umfassen: - Unterstützung im Lizenzmanagement: Du unterstützt das Lizenz-Team bei der Pflege und Koordination der Beziehungen zu internationalen Lizenzpartnern.
- Mitarbeit an internationalen Projekten: Du begleitest internationale Lizenzprojekte über verschiedene Phasen hinweg – von den ersten Gesprächen über den Vertragsabschluss bis hin zur Produktentwicklung und dem Marktstart.
- Kaufmännische Unterstützung: Du hilfst bei der Erstellung und Pflege von Lizenz-GuVs (Gewinn- und Verlustrechnungen) und unterstützt bei der Ausarbeitung von Berichten sowie Präsentationen für interne Stakeholder.
- Schnittstellenkoordination: Du unterstützt die Kommunikation zwischen internen Fachbereichen (z. B. Produktentwicklung, Marketing, Recht, Finanzen) und externen Lizenzagenturen oder -partnern.
- Markt- & Branchenrecherche: Du recherchierst aktuelle Trends sowie Entwicklungen in der globalen Lizenz- und Unterhaltungsbranche und bereitest die Ergebnisse für das Team auf.

Was wir uns von dir wünschen: - Studium: Immatrikulierte/r Student/in, idealerweise in Betriebswirtschaftslehre (BWL), Medienmanagement, Kommunikationswissenschaften oder einem verwandten Studiengang.
- Brancheninteresse: Erste Berührungspunkte mit oder Interesse an der globalen Spielzeug- und Unterhaltungsindustrie.
- Zahlenaffinität: Grundlegendes Verständnis kaufmännischer Konzepte sowie ein sicherer Umgang mit Excel und Berichten.
- Vorerfahrung von Vorteil: Praktika oder Tätigkeiten als Werkstudent/in im Bereich Lizenzierung, Marketing oder Business Development sind von Vorteil, aber kein Muss.
- Kommunikationsstärke: Gute Kommunikations- und Präsentationsfähigkeiten in Deutsch und Englisch sowie ein selbstsicheres Auftreten im Kontakt mit externen Partnern.
- Persönlichkeit: Proaktive, strukturierte und lernbegierige Persönlichkeit, die gerne eigenverantwortlich arbeitet und sich in einem internationalen, dynamischen Umfeld wohlfühlt.

Warum tonies? - Globales Teamwork: Wir arbeiten über Abteilungs- und Ländergrenzen hinweg an unserer Vision, die Toniebox in jedes Kinderzimmer der Welt zu bringen.
- Come as you are: Das gilt nicht nur für den Dresscode, sondern für alles andere auch. Denn nur wo du dich wirklich wohlfühlst, kannst du dein Bestes geben.
- Sprachen lernen & Entspannung: Verbessere deine Kommunikationsfähigkeiten mit der Sprachlern-App Babbel und finde Entspannung durch unseren Zugang zur Meditations-App Calm.
- Urlaubspaket: Genieße 30 Tage Jahresurlaub (basierend auf einer 5-Tage-Woche) sowie zusätzliche freie Tage an Heiligabend, Silvester und Rosenmontag.

Gut zu wissen: Bei tonies® sind Inklusion und Vielfalt fest in unseren Grundprinzipien verankert. Wir schätzen die vielfältigen Talente, Hintergründe, Überzeugungen und Geschlechtsidentitäten, die unter unserem Dach zusammenkommen. Jedes Gesicht ist willkommen, und wir unterstützen jeden Menschen in allen Phasen seiner Entwicklung bei uns.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung!

title: Provider Credentialing and Practice Lead
description:
Mission 

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose 

The Clinical Practicec Lead owns practice management for Neko Health's United States professional corporation. The role covers four areas: provider credentialing, SOP organization and maintenance, onboarding operationalization, and compliance assurance. Neko runs a tech-enabled clinical model, and this role is expected to run all four through systems and automation rather than manual tracking.

Credentialing: the role holds the credential file for every provider practicing under the PC: license, certification, permitted scope by state, malpractice coverage details and every other expirable, verified at source and kept current so that no provider ever sees a member on a lapsed credential. While Neko does not credential with payers today - this role runs the credentialing gate that clears a provider to practice and removes that clearance when a credential lapses. It supplies provider credentialing data into the clinic compliance systems and works to the credentialing standard and clear-to-practice definition set by the Head of Compliance.

SOPs: the role owns the SOP library for US practice operations. The role keeps every SOP current, versioned, and easy to find, and retires SOPs that no longer apply.

Onboarding: the role turns each new provider's onboarding plan into a working, tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start, in the right order and against a clear timeline.

Compliance: the role checks that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance, and reports gaps as they surface.

Systems and automation: the role chooses, configures and owns the tooling that carries all of the above — one source of truth for provider data, automated expiry alerts, and workflows that hand off cleanly between Talent Acquisition, the People Team, IT and clinical operations. Status should be visible from the system rather than assembled by hand.

As Neko opens further states, credentialing volume and complexity grow faster than headcount, and practice operations grow with them. This role exists to make provider readiness, SOP currency, onboarding execution, and compliance standing a managed process with evidence behind it, built on tooling that scales faster than headcount, rather than a scramble before each launch.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months 

- A current, auditable register of every clinician's license, credential, and permitted scope by state, held in a single system of record with automated expiry tracking and a named process for renewal before lapse.

- A complete credential file per provider practicing under the PC, with primary source verification evidence attached and dated.

- A written credentialing procedure covering intake, verification, the clear-to-practice decision, re-verification cycle, and removal of clearance.

- The credentialing gate built into the clinician onboarding sequence, so a start date cannot be confirmed without verified credentials.

- A current SOP library for US practice operations: indexed, version-controlled, and reviewed on a set cycle.

- An onboarding operations sequence that turns each new provider's plan into a tracked timeline from offer to start, with the credentialing gate built in.

- Practice operations running in-system rather than on spreadsheets: onboarding, SOP review cycles and compliance checks tracked in Neko's tooling, with the remaining manual steps documented and a plan to remove them.

- A compliance status report showing where US practice operations meet the Head of Compliance's standards, and where they do not, generated from the system rather than compiled by hand.

Key Responsibilities 

Provider credentialing and primary source verification 

- Run credentialing intake for every new provider joining the PC: application, document collection, and verification at source rather than from candidate-supplied copies.

- Verify state medical/nursing licenses, board certification, education and training, work history, and DEA registration where the provider's scope requires it.

- Operate the clear-to-practice gate: no provider is released to see members until the credential file is complete and verified.

- Maintain the permitted scope by state for each provider and flag to the Head of Compliance any request to practice outside it.

Expirables, re-verification and removal 

- Own the expirables calendar for licenses, certifications, DEA registrations, malpractice coverage and any other time-limited credential, driven by automated alerts rather than manual review.

- Chase renewals ahead of expiry against defined lead times and escalate when a renewal is at risk.

- Remove clearance to practice immediately when a credential lapses and notify the clinical rota owner and the Head of Compliance the same day.

- Run the re-verification cycle so credential files do not silently age.

Systems, tooling and automation 

- Select, implement and administer the tooling that runs practice operations: credentialing records, expiry tracking, onboarding workflow and SOP version control.

- Replace manual tracking with automated alerts, scheduled reporting and system-driven handoffs, and keep a running list of the steps still done by hand.

- Define the data structure behind credentialing and onboarding so status can be reported out of the system rather than reconstructed.

- Work with IT and, where relevant, product and engineering to integrate practice operations data with adjacent systems instead of maintaining parallel spreadsheets.

SOP organization and maintenance 

- Own the SOP library for US practice operations: create, index, and version every procedure.

- Review each SOP on a set cycle and update it when a process changes.

- Retire SOPs that no longer apply, and flag processes that run without one.

- Keep SOPs easy to find and use for the staff who rely on them day to day.

Onboarding operationalization 

- Turn each new provider's onboarding plan into a tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start.

- Own the onboarding timeline from offer to start date, and flag delays before they hit the start date.

- Coordinate with Talent Acquisition, the People Team, and clinical operations to keep the sequence moving.

- Improve the onboarding sequence as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders.

Compliance assurance 

- Confirm that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance.

- Run periodic checks against those standards, and report gaps as they surface.

- Support audits of practice operations with evidence drawn from SOPs, onboarding records, and the credentialing file.

- Escalate compliance gaps that need action beyond this role.

Credentialing process, data and reporting 

- Keep the credentialing record system accurate and audit-ready, so a credential file can be produced on request without reconstruction.

- Report credentialing status, upcoming expiries and blocked providers into the Medical Quality reporting cycle, on a set cadence and drawn from the system of record.

- Improve the credentialing process as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders.

- Prepare the function for payer credentialing and provider enrollment should Neko US move to billing insurance.

About you 

Minimum Requirements 

- Experience streamlining clinical or healthcare operations in a tech-enabled environment: you have taken a manual, spreadsheet-run process and rebuilt it as a system-driven workflow, and you can describe what you removed and what changed as a result.

- Experience working in a clinical operations capacity – where you were responsible for not just executing but building the systems to ensure credentialing, compliance and other clinical operations processes are handled excellently.

- Confident with operational tooling: you configure and administer the systems you depend on rather than raising a ticket for every change, and you are comfortable working with data, reporting and everyday automation.

- Direct, hands-on experience of state medical board licensure and clinician credentialing processes, including primary source verification.

- Experience maintaining a credentialing database or record system to an audit-ready standard.

- Experience developing, organizing, and maintaining SOPs in a clinical or regulated operations setting.

- Working knowledge of compliance standards in a healthcare or clinical operations setting, with experience checking operations against them.

- Precise and persistent administratively

Preferred 

- Experience in a digital health, telehealth or otherwise tech-enabled care setting, where clinical operations run on product and tooling rather than paper.

- Hands-on experience with credentialing or provider data platforms, and with the workflow and tracking tools used to run operations day to day.

- Experience working alongside product or engineering teams to specify what operational tooling needs to do.

- Direct experience provider credentialing in a United States clinical setting, including multi-state credentialing.

- Experience of credentialing in a newly opened market or a start-up clinical service where the process did not yet exist.

- Experience building an SOP program from scratch in a growing or newly opened operation.

Compensation and Benefits 

- Paid Time Off & Holidays

- Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance

- 401(k) Retirement Plan

- Commuter Benefits

- Wellness Rewards Program

- Complimentary full Neko scan for you and eligible family members

Compensation: $137K – $167K

title: Founding Sales (Munich Office)
description:
Founding Sales

About Dataleap 

We raised $3M from YC and angels like Aravind (CEO Perplexity) and Rahul Vohra (Superhuman) to build the agentic operating system for the enterprise. We have thousands of agents deployed across scale-up startups and Fortune 500 companies. We have PMF and are doubling revenue every month. And we have far more enterprise inbound than we can handle.

About the role 

Until now, I've closed every deal at Dataleap myself. I need someone to do it better than I do.

You'll work directly with me, the CEO and founder, across the full sales lifecycle, from the first cold email to the signed contract. You'll also take over a large and growing pile of inbound leads and demo requests that we can't keep up with today.

As our founding sales hire, you won't be handed a playbook. You'll write it. Every pitch, objection and closed deal shapes how Dataleap sells for years. As we scale, you'll help hire and build the sales team underneath you. 

You'll also have a front-row seat to AI. You'll sell the product that is changing how enterprises operate, and you'll use it to change how sales works.

What you'll do 

- Outbound: Find our ideal customers and get them on the phone. Grow our outbound motion from zero into a repeatable engine.

- Inbound: Demo and close the warm prospects who come through our front door. Turn interest into signed contracts, fast.

- Events: Host events for prospects and customers, from intimate executive dinners to agent hackathons, so people walk away wanting to work with us.

- Systems: Own the source of truth for our sales data. Build the pipeline, processes and reporting we'll need to grow this team 10x.

- Agents: Build your own set of Dataleap agents to scale yourself. We expect you to cut manual work out of your job systematically, not to use AI as a productivity boost.

- Be the voice of the market: Bring what you hear from buyers back to product and engineering. Push for what customers need, and push back when they're wrong.

- Find the thousand things I haven't listed here, and just do them.

You're a fit if 

- You're a closer. You've carried a number and hit it, ideally selling complex software to enterprise or fast-growing companies. You know how to run a multi-stakeholder deal from champion to procurement.

- You're a hunter. You don't wait for leads. You enjoy outbound, find creative ways into accounts, and can't stand a quiet pipeline.

- You're an AI power user. You don't just "explore AI", you live in it. You can demo agents credibly because you build them yourself, and you can hold your own with a CTO.

- You're high agency and fast. You set the agenda, prioritize ruthlessly, and communicate clearly and to the point.

- You're low ego and high ownership. Some of the work isn't glamorous, like cleaning the CRM or chasing a signature at 11pm, and you do it anyway. You want to work hard and be obsessed with what you do.

- You build systems. You can't help turning chaos into process, and you think about how the next ten reps will sell, not just how you will.

- You speak German at a native level and are based in Munich (or ready to move here).

What you get 

- A first-hand view of how a YC company goes from founder-led sales to a scaled revenue engine, with you building it.

- Direct exposure to the best people at YC, Founders Inc and CDTM.

- Frequent trips to San Francisco to keep you at the frontier of agentic AI.

- The best mentors and coaches for whatever problem you're working on.

- An unlimited AI budget to automate your own work.

- Generous equity and a compensation package (base plus uncapped commission) that reflects the impact I expect this role to have.

- The path to build and lead the sales team as we scale.

- I will personally make sure this is the fastest growth opportunity of your career.

- If you ever want to start your own company, I'll back you.

description:
Would you like to maintain more than just another technical system and work with a technology that is truly unique worldwide? ⚡ 

Our client is a fast growing GreenTech startup developing one of the world’s first scalable road based power plants. The technology uses existing road infrastructure to generate renewable energy from passing traffic without requiring any additional land.

As a Maintenance Technician in Hamburg , you will be responsible for the technical operation and maintenance of the road based power plant installed there. You will ensure reliable operation, carry out maintenance and repairs, and systematically investigate technical faults.

You will not simply follow existing procedures. Since this is an entirely new technology, you will actively help shape how maintenance, service, and technical support processes are developed for the future . Your hands on experience from daily operations will directly contribute to the continued development of the service structure.

Your Benefits

• Unique technology: Work with the world’s first road based power plant in active operation and contribute to a GreenTech solution that currently exists nowhere else in this form.

• Real opportunity to shape processes: Develop maintenance schedules, service processes, and maintenance structures together with the team instead of simply following existing procedures.

• Flexible part time schedule: Work 20 to 30 hours per week with flexible working hours that can easily be combined with university studies or other commitments.

• Independent work: Take responsibility for the technical operation of the plant in Hamburg and enjoy a high degree of autonomy when it comes to maintenance, troubleshooting, and repairs.

• Development opportunities: Grow together with the technology and take on additional responsibility for operations and service as your experience increases.

• Attractive compensation: Receive competitive compensation based on your qualifications and practical experience.

Your Responsibilities

As a Maintenance Technician , you will help ensure the reliable technical operation of the road based power plant in Hamburg.

• Maintenance and repairs: Inspect and maintain the system across mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical components. Your responsibilities will also include tasks such as monitoring and maintaining the hydraulic oil.

• Troubleshooting: Analyse technical issues, resolve faults, and document both the solution and the underlying cause.

• Service development: Create and continuously improve maintenance schedules, spare parts lists, and technical service documentation for the system.

• Spare parts management: Keep track of spare parts stored on site and ensure they are managed in a structured and reliable way.

Your Profile as a Maintenance Technician

• You have a technical background in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, energy technology , or a comparable technical qualification.

• You have practical experience in the mechanical maintenance and repair of technical systems or machinery.

• You have a solid understanding of hydraulic systems and are able to independently understand technical relationships and identify potential issues.

• You are available for 20 to 30 hours per week and are flexible enough to occasionally work early mornings, evenings, or weekends when suitable maintenance windows are available at the terminal.

• You enjoy taking responsibility, work independently, and remain calm and solution oriented when dealing with technical problems.

• You enjoy working directly on technical equipment and outdoors and feel comfortable in an active traffic and logistics environment.

• The ability to confidently read technical drawings, hydraulic schematics, and electrical circuit diagrams is an advantage.

Would you like to do more than simply maintain a globally unique GreenTech system and actively help shape how its future operation and service structure are developed? ⚡

- Open Source: Entwickle bestehende Systeme konsequent weiter und begleite Migrationen von Standardsoftware zu geeigneten Open Source Alternativen.

- Kenntnisse in der Automatisierung , beispielsweise mit Python, Ansible oder vergleichbaren Technologien. 

- Begeisterung für Open Source und Interesse daran, eine IT-Landschaft langfristig auf offenen und sicheren Lösungen aufzubauen. 

- Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse auf mindestens C1 Niveau sowie fließende Englischkenntnisse. 

- Eigenständige, pragmatische Arbeitsweise und Lust darauf, technische Entscheidungen aktiv mitzugestalten und gemeinsam im Team neue Lösungen auszuprobieren. 

- Kenntnisse in Nextcloud, Open Xchange, Nginx, pfSense, OpenVPN, Git oder Ceph sowie Erfahrung mit IT Security sind von Vorteil.
